assessments.summary: Assessment of the locked canonical PDF at C:\Users\lluis\Documents\Codex\2026-08-10\ade\work\arr-deposit-rank-adaptive-20260830\papers\2026\08\7N\ARR-2026-7NPRNBW4488HG90K\paper.pdf. The manuscript appears mathematically sound on its main claims. I found no unresolved objection that would invalidate the one-spike inverse formula, optimizer singular rigidity, stability theorem, or exact triangular/quadrilateral loop laws. The appropriate disposition is minor revision, mainly for reproducibility metadata, clearer Horn-theorem exposition, and more independently verifiable novelty/provenance support.
strengths: The reduction from Hermitian factor products to a one-matrix self-commutator minimization is clean, dimensionally consistent, and handles balancing and attainment.
The one-spike formula is supported by a concise Horn lower bound and an explicit weighted-shift construction, with zero-padding handled correctly.
The singular-value rigidity conclusion follows from equality in the summed lower bounds and is stronger than mere cost evaluation.
The stability theorem has sharp constants and equality families, and the strict Schur-concavity corollary follows correctly from prefix-sum majorization.

The three-kick and four-kick loop theorems correctly reduce fixed-target polygon synthesis to the inverse commutator cost, and the four-kick Gram-determinant correction avoids the false parallelogram inequality.
weaknesses: The Horn step is correct but under-explained; readers not already fluent with Horn triples and partition indexing may have to reconstruct a key convention-dependent inequality.
The novelty and priority discussion is cautious, but it depends heavily on author-side records and an accompanying audit that is not included in the exact PDF.
The reproducibility section asserts accompanying exact-arithmetic routes but does not give enough bibliographic or computational metadata to locate or rerun them from the PDF alone.

The paper does not classify all optimizing matrices, solve the general mixed-sign spectral problem, or give exact formulas for five or more kicks; these limitations are stated, but they bound the practical reach of the work.

Possible nonmaterial reproducibility risk: the claimed accompanying implementation cannot be verified from the exact PDF because no package locator, hash, or command transcript is supplied.

Possible nonmaterial provenance risk: the exact ARR self-citations and priority audit were not independently discoverable from the PDF alone or simple public search, so novelty confidence is lower than correctness confidence.
Possible terminology risk: S_2 denotes a sum of Hilbert-Schmidt norms rather than quadratic edge energy; the manuscript defines it clearly, but readers may initially misread the notation.

Rigidity of the nonzero squared singular values 2 sum_{j=l}^n b_j and rank n for every balanced optimum on that cone.

assessments.summary: Evaluación favorable con revisiones menores de trazabilidad y bibliografía, sin objeciones materiales pendientes. Leí la fuente completa y las 15 páginas del PDF canónico, verifiqué su SHA-256 y revisé todos los argumentos y los siete programas: :codex-file-citation{path="C:/Users/lluis/Documents/Codex/2026-09-05/files-pasted-by-the-user-soy/outputs/inertia_revision3_submission/paper.pdf" purpose="source"}. Contrasté la formulación y la indexación de Horn en Fulton, sin auditar su demostración completa. Las consultas directas a los cuatro registros ARR [1,2,9,10] no pudieron recuperarse mediante la herramienta; no realicé una búsqueda amplia ni confirmé prioridad. Las comprobaciones finitas apoyan los argumentos, pero no sustituyen la prueba para todas las multiplicidades. El resumen del artículo refleja lo demostrado y declara los problemas abiertos. El modelo participó en producir el manuscrito: este contexto nuevo sigue siendo revisión interna de IA, no arbitraje humano independiente. No modifiqué el manuscrito ni los certificados bloqueados, ni publiqué ni contacté a terceros.
strengths: Teorema 1: la descomposición espectral comparte una cámara ordenada; el término positivo alpha_m beta_n da estrictitud, y la semicontinuidad con la fórmula de una espiga establece el supremo en cada estrato.

Teoremas 2–3: la identidad polinómica de la sección 5.2 y sus signos cubren todas las multiplicidades no equilibradas. Sustituir la última cota de Horn por s_n>=b_n produce correctamente el coeficiente inverso (n-1)/2.

Teorema 4: las dos triangulaciones y el corte q(a)=q(b) dan ocho celdas con D_* afín y exactamente 22 vértices. La maximización de la función convexa kappa_d+(17/36)D_* en sus vértices es válida con H=2 fijo.

La convención de índices y la suficiencia utilizadas corresponden a las ecuaciones (8)–(10) y al Teorema 1 de [Fulton](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9908012). La regeneración por tableaux aporta un control distinto del generador recursivo, aunque ambos programas pertenecen al mismo proceso de revisión interna.
En (r,p), la cota sum_j max(a_j,b_j)=31/24 coincide con el testigo superior. La perturbación de p mantiene inercia (3,3) y fuerza el cociente 17/36 para cualquier d fijo>=6.

Teorema 5 y Corolario 5.2: se distingue correctamente el óptimo del transporte del coste matricial; el ejemplo 3/2 frente a 4/3 da exactamente un 12,5% de separación. El umbral de pureza de signo 1/2 se deduce de la estrictitud y tiene la familia límite requerida.
weaknesses: Conviene añadir localizadores de teorema o página para las atribuciones específicas a [1,2,9,10] y una correspondencia explícita entre enunciados actuales y certificados. La prioridad queda abierta; la imposibilidad de recuperar esos enlaces en esta revisión no demuestra que estén rotos.

La contribución de transporte utiliza mecanismos clásicos y testigos que pueden ser subóptimos; su utilidad no equivale a una fórmula del coste general. El manuscrito reconoce adecuadamente esta limitación.
La optimalidad equilibrada hacia delante solo queda resuelta aquí para N=2,3; la clasificación de casi extremizadores para N>=4 utiliza constantes positivas sin afirmar que sean óptimas.

assessments.summary: Primera evaluación científica sustantiva de Born en esta tarea, para el PDF v004 identificado por su hash. El argumento de transversabilidad prueba un único pliegue y permite cerrar el contacto positivo único, la clasificación global y la RDF de dos piezas bajo el modelo declarado. Se comprobó la dependencia BP y su reparación, la segunda vía exacta de signos y la reproducibilidad descrita. No quedó identificada una objeción material pendiente; recomiendo accept, Millennium 4,30. La novedad se limita frente a los antecedentes efectivamente consultados. Astra participó en preparación y no reclama independencia estadística. Este dictamen no constituye aceptación editorial. Esta respuesta ratifica el dictamen v004 conservado y lo vincula al recibo SUB-A453B172DDBA71F0 tras comprobar de nuevo el mismo hash; no representa una nueva revisión científica.

Las tablas de alta precisión y los controles de mallas son evidencia numérica, sin aritmética de intervalos ni certificación del mínimo global por sí solos.

assessments.summary: I find the manuscript's new core argument convincing: the first-order Kummer equation reduces the fold numerator to a rational phase-plane comparison, the transversality signs force exactly one fold, and the subsequent stationary/global-maximizer analysis gives a unique contact with no reentrance. Combined with the restated envelope interface, this yields the claimed two-piece RDF; the d=2 specialization agrees with the Dytso–Cardone sphere formula. The exact coefficient theorem and all reproduction checks also passed. The principal residual dependence is the external Brazitikos–Pandis power-sum extremum, whose arXiv v1 proof contains a real arithmetic error; the manuscript identifies it and supplies a correct replacement for the affected range. I found no unresolved material objection.

The one-change coefficient theorem uses 66 finite exact comparisons for 3<=d<=35 rather than a wholly uniform analytic argument, although those comparisons are non-floating-point and fully exposed.
The numerical tables are high-precision consistency evidence rather than interval-certified enclosures, but no theorem proof depends on their decimal values.

correctness_confidence.basis: Lemmas 1-4 provide the necessary operational reduction, central-block nullity bound, order-three square rigidity and line-union classification. The proof observes the strict 7d/9 cutoff, cyclic representation and nonzero trinomial coefficients. Central multiplicity and circle-intersection arguments are terse but sufficient on inspection.

The predecessor is unavailable within the allowed review scope, and priority remains unestablished.

reproducibility.basis: Independent enumeration of all 4095 line subsets, exact integer-pair matrix arithmetic in d=9,27,81 and all 6320 ordered label pairs in d=9 support the finite claims. The claimed ternary_verify.py, certificate and reading ledger were not included and were not executed.

assessments.summary: Assessment of the exact 9-page v1 PDF: the low-rank classification appears correct under the explicitly fixed cyclic Weyl representation d=3^k,k>=2 and strict rank<7d/9 condition. All pages and displayed formulas were read. The core argument genuinely constrains arbitrary positive sparse factorizations, rather than merely exhibiting 150 examples. Theorem B distinguishes list size from sparse-square length and proves the exact-rank increase; Theorem C supplies an operator-level counterexample at the cutoff. No unresolved material objection was identified. Minor revision is recommended for reproducibility and source accessibility. The 3.7 score recognizes a strong specialized classification with bounded broader significance and unverified priority.
strengths: W-S1 | Lemma 1, p. 3: the vectorization convention and partial-trace transpose give sum B_j^*B_j=d I_r in the necessity direction, hence C_j=A B_j^*/sqrt(d). Conversely A^+C_j and the 1/d Weyl twirl yield a normalized POVM with the specified support lists. Label inversion/phases preserve sparsity; the channel interpretation is not inferred from rank alone.

W-S2 | Lemma 2, p. 4: the 3-adic coordinate reduction makes the central subgroup order d/q, so each central sector has dimension q rather than an unaccounted repeated multiplicity. Nonzero shift weights give nullity exactly one in a singular sector. With a,b,c nonzero, the determinant-zero condition is an intersection of distinct circles, allowing at most two central-character pairs. The crucial subgroup count passed for all 5616 noncommuting ordered distinct nonzero label pairs in dimension nine.

W-S3 | Lemma 3, pp. 4-5: rank<7d/9 excludes noncommuting trinomials because d-2>=7d/9 for d>=9. A commuting group of order h>=9 similarly gives rank>=d-2d/h. Thus the relative support must reduce to an order-three algebra, and CC^* is a nonnegative combination of at most two parallel line projectors. Right multiplication preserves CC^*, so the resulting fixed ambient algebra is not lost in normalizing the sparse factor.

W-S4 | Lemma 4 and Theorem A, pp. 5-6: positivity makes support exactly a union of character cells. Independent enumeration of all 4095 nonempty line subsets gives 12 singletons,54 crossing pairs,12 parallel pairs and72 triangles with union size below seven, and verifies both no hidden lines and a private point on every constituent. Private-cell values recover the weights uniquely, including when unordered eigenvalues coincide.

W-S5 | Theorem A, pp. 2,6: each individual sparse square can use only parallel lines. Crossing pairs and triangles therefore require respectively two and three squares, whereas a parallel pair can be combined into one factor. This establishes the stated minimal lengths, not just upper bounds. Exact integer-pair arithmetic verified all nine scaled cell projectors, twelve scaled line projectors and 66 pair intersections per dimension in d=9,27,81.

W-S6 | Theorem B and Corollary 5, pp. 7-8: singular order-three binomial squares are flat complements, forcing the twelve equal-weight parallel midpoints as the only two-list states below the cutoff. The four-term (I-U)(I-V) has square nine on exactly four cells, rank4d/9 and trace4d; the square/trace identity was checked exactly in all three dimensions. The rank-seven two-list obstruction in d=9 correctly uses the common kernel of positive sums.

W-S7 | Theorem C, p. 8: (T-I)(T-xi I) with T=Z^(d/9) has exactly two zero order-nine eigenvalues and hence rank7d/9. Its nonzero T^2 coefficient lies outside the order-three label subgroup, proving failure of the fixed-algebra conclusion at equality. This is a valid sharpness example for the structural statement, not a classification of every state at or above the cutoff.
weaknesses: W-W1 | Section 7 and reference [1], pp. 8-9: ternary_verify.py, ternary_certificate.json and the predecessor reading ledger are not in the supplied ZIP. The predecessor was not sought in project history or other contexts. Its claimed rank-law priority and the manuscript-specific hash binding of the original replay remain unverified, even though the needed argument is reproduced in Lemmas 2-3.

W-W2 | References [2]-[6], p. 9: the general learning-width/factor-width correspondence is explicitly present in Johnston et al., Lemma 9 and Corollary 11 [https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20789v1]. Character-space size and Weyl block structure have the cited precedents [https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.1519; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2101.00129]. These sources support the ingredients, not priority of the 150-family positive-sum classification. Gross and Veitch et al. were checked only at abstract level, not at all cited sections.

W-W3 | pp. 1-2,8-9: the commuting rank-d/3 projectors belong to a single cyclic d-dimensional representation. They cannot be identified as operators with twelve pure qutrit stabilizer states or carried unchanged to a tensor-product Pauli sparsity problem. The paper states this correctly; it materially narrows possible generalizations.

W-W4 | pp. 3-8: finite enumeration certifies the nine-point incidence geometry, not all complex sparse coefficients or every k. The latter depend on the analytic circle and central-sector arguments. No formalization or numerical search over all coefficients was performed, and no stability statement under approximate zeros is proved.

Theorem A: unique decomposition into line states together with exact minimal three-sparse-square length for each family.

Theorem B: the exact fixed-state two/three-list distinction and ell_min_exact(d,4d/9)=4 versus ell_min_exact(d,5d/9)=3. The incidence geometry and operational factor-width principle themselves are antecedents.

assessments.summary: Assessment of the exact 13-page v1 PDF: the claimed complete one-state forward and inverse laws are supported by explicit feasible constructions and matching lower certificates. All equations were read from rendered pages. The positivity-active branch addresses a real failure of the inactive lower bound, and the inverse proof correctly restricts a feasible one-parameter family that contains the established optimizer. No unresolved main-theorem objection was identified. Minor revision is recommended to make the claimed replay available and improve the standalone presentation and citation precision. A 3.5 score reflects a substantive, unusually explicit result of narrow scope; this is a research assessment, not an editorial decision.
strengths: R-S1 | Sections 1-2, pp. 1-4: for a nonconstant degree-one inner matrix, the determinant contributes a single Poisson-kernel trace delay with minimum possible peak one. This explains the jump at T=1 and the constant optimum 1/2 below it. The Cayley denominator ellipse is equivalent to the eigenvalue-ratio constraint, not an uncalibrated surrogate for angular delay.

R-S2 | Section 2, equations (5)-(7), pp. 3-4: every extra-port router yields nonnegative Q and P=H-Q satisfying the necessary node inequalities. Factoring a feasible pair and completing two scalar numerators gives a two-port realization, so the lower certificates apply to arbitrary N>=2 without a hidden truncation assumption.

R-S3 | Sections 3-4, pp. 4-5: interpolation gives the inactive lower bound; (A prime D-A D prime) prime=A double-prime D+2A>0 isolates its minimizer. Equation (10) reduces residual PSD to B>=-v. The support comparison at tau and decreasing U_c account for the single finite transition exactly when u>3v, including cases where the square root defining U_c is unavailable.

R-S4 | Section 5, pp. 5-7: the active construction has Q=k(s-t)^2, P=e(s-r)^2 and H=(s-v)^2+L^2. The positive endpoint weights and polynomial identity (19) yield a contradiction for every smaller candidate error. Equality fixes H, Q and all three active nodes; at the boundary nu=0 the remaining rank-one and leading-coefficient conditions still establish uniqueness.

R-S5 | Exact independent check of the p. 9 active fixture: T=2,v=9/20,u=1399/180 yields lambda_minus=3/16, lambda_plus=13/16, nu=2/123 and lambda_0=182077/17280. Coefficient matching in (19), the first-moment identity (20), and all node equalities hold in rational arithmetic. The transition fixture u=165/28 gives t=tau=-15/16 and e=9/25 exactly.

R-S6 | Section 6, pp. 7-8: |h_0|^2-|h_1|^2=4*Delta>0 places denominator zeros outside the closed disk; the sharp-polynomial completion is unitary on the boundary with determinant h_z sharp/h_z of degree one, including h_1=0. Across 400 independent parameter cases (253 inactive,147 active), 17 circle evaluations each gave maximum unitarity residual 4.45e-15 and node residual 2.0e-15. These samples support the algebra, not a replacement for its continuum proof.

R-S7 | Section 7, pp. 8-10: u=3,v=1/3,T=2 gives active e=0.250257935326986 versus inactive lower bound 0.250029973086878, confirming that the latter is unattainable. The symmetry, T=1 jump and fixed-gap asymptotic regimes are consistent with the formulas; the fourth-order discrepancy has the claimed positive coefficient d^2(u-3v)^2/4.

R-S8 | Theorem 2, pp. 10-12: (31)-(32) show that |y|<=d/g is exactly residual positivity, with H positive definite. The cubic derivative sign and endpoint truncation identify the minimum of the delay parameter. At u=2,v=1,epsilon=35/123, G(1/4)=0, B=-9/70 and C=223/70 were verified exactly. Independent scalar minimization of the inverse family agreed with the forward cap over all 400 cases within 1.08e-7 relative error, including the T=1 endpoint.

Those statements provide no independent evidence for the present assessment and were not followed into project history. Novelty over those local predecessors remains unverified; the standalone formulas and proofs were assessed directly.

R-W2 | Section 9, p. 13: the cited structural and convexification precedents are real and relevant. Alpay-Jorgensen-Lewkowicz, Theorems 2.3 and 3.1, cover degree-preserving completion and rank-one factors [https://arxiv.org/html/1410.0283v2]; Wu-Boyd-Vandenberghe describe magnitude-square convexification [https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/magdes.html]. These established ingredients should not contribute to an unsupported claim of broad novelty.

The Zhang et al. comparison was checked only against its primary abstract. Neither check excludes earlier results equivalent to the exact routing phase law, and no exhaustive priority search was performed.

R-W4 | Sections 6,7,9: the software mentioned in the PDF is absent from the batch. The independent checks here reconstruct formulas, not the author implementation. Floating-point sampling does not certify arbitrary algebraic inputs, node-collision limits or all coefficients; exact general validity rests on the printed proofs.

R-W5 | Model and Section 9: phase-free orthogonal targets and exact degree one are essential. The explicit matrix compiler is not a physical component synthesis, and the high-delay expansions require fixed positive gaps. The manuscript acknowledges these restrictions, which constrain the result's significance.

assessments.summary: Assessment of the exact 14-page v1 PDF: a strong, specialized mathematical contribution with a credible proof chain from weak spectral selection to exact eventual two-block rigidity and unrestricted high-fidelity rate-distortion. All pages, including both appendices, were read. The moment selectors, spectral/radial separation, covariance, posterior mean and complement rescaling survive the checks performed. Lemma 2.3 has a demonstrably insufficient equality condition and equation (37) misses a Gaussian factor; both are local corrections because maximization is separately supplied in Theorem 5.2 and the high-rate constant is independently normalized in Proposition 5.1. Recommend minor revision as a research assessment. The score 4.0 denotes a strong result on the supplied comparison scale, not Millennium-level significance or a probability of correctness.
strengths: G-S1 | Lemmas 2.2 and 2.3, pp. 3-4: conditional Hilbert-Schmidt least squares and data processing justify restricting arbitrary reports to 0 <= sigma <= I/r, tr(sigma)=1. The relative-entropy inequality itself is correct and does not assume that reconstructions remain pure orbit points.

G-S2 | Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.3, pp. 4-5,13: beta moments give the stated quadratic/cubic coefficients; the cubic extremum has one positive spike, and the balanced negative quartic selects equal positive/negative blocks. Exact rational checks covered 304 beta identities for d=3,...,18 and balanced Schur coefficients for even d=4,...,18. Within-block symmetry keeps these spectra stationary under the invariant perturbation.

G-S3 | Lemmas 4.1-4.2 and Theorem 4.3, pp. 5-6,11-12: the strict cross-gap supplies a unique maximizing plane even with internal eigenvalue collisions. Fixed cutoffs, exponentially small exterior/annular contributions and Gaussian polynomial domination support C2 control. On the labeled trace-zero sphere, Hess(h_r)=-h_r/R^2 times the metric; this makes the large-s optimizer exactly two-block, beyond mere asymptotic convergence.

G-S4 | Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.5, pp. 6-7: incompatible weak/strong unique orbits and the analytic identity theorem force failure of real analyticity at finite field. The first-exit coexistence-or-degeneracy alternative follows from compact separation and local strictness. The physical-radius bound satisfies both eigenvalue constraints. No claim of a first-order or unique transition is needed.

G-S5 | Theorem 5.2 and Theorem 6.1, pp. 7-8: radial localization keeps maximizers away from zero; exact fixed-radius optimality reduces the complete physical-body dual to b S_Q. The inward boundary derivative and large-lambda radial concavity produce an interior maximizer. Haar covariance gives the correct source marginal, and equation (25) yields the posterior-mean report. Thus the stronger, corrected equality condition in G1 is met here.

G-S6 | Proposition 5.1, Corollary 6.2 and Proposition 6.3, pp. 7-9: independent exact Hankel-determinant ratios verified all 81 (d,r) cases with 2<=d<=18 and r<=d/2. K_5,2=144. Direct Jacobi quadrature reproduced the crossing s=4.8585790529165 and all three Table 2 rows. The coefficient r(d-r), distortion rescaling r^2/(d-r)^2, and Born-query factor 1/[d(d+1)] are consistent.
weaknesses: G-W1 | pp. 9-11: D_*(d,r) and the large-field threshold are existential. The listed kappa=20,40,80 values are verified channel values, not certified points inside the unrestricted-optimality interval. The paper appropriately acknowledges this, but it substantially limits numerical deployment of the exact theorem.

G-W2 | pp. 1-2,10,13-14: the checked prior work supports the distinction between fixed-d spectrum optimization, orbit-restricted coding and ambient reconstruction. In particular, Dytso-Cardone already solve ambient squared-error sphere rate-distortion [https://arxiv.org/html/2401.04248v1], while Harremoes uses the group as both alphabets [https://arxiv.org/pdf/0901.0015]. These comparisons do not establish that no earlier Grassmann spectral-optimization theorem exists.

G-W3 | p. 11: the named replay archive and scripts are not supplied in this batch. Independent calculations here are distinct from that archive; its digest, script contents and claimed coverage were not verified. No formal proof verification or all-parameter numerical certification was performed.
potential_errors: G1 | Confirmed local error, Lemma 2.3, p. 4: constancy of Q_lambda on report support is insufficient for equality in (5); it must equal the global supremum there. Counterexample: d=2,r=1,lambda=10 and constant A=0. The stated Gibbs posterior is Haar and Q is constant, yet I+lambda D=5. A source-orbit report has Q=(1-exp(-20))/20, so the right side of (5) is at most 2.9957322756, strictly below 5. Theorem 6.1 is not invalidated because Theorem 5.2 separately establishes that its reports maximize Q.

G2 | Confirmed local normalization error, Appendix A.3 equation (37), p. 12: with dW explicitly ordinary real-coordinate Lebesgue measure in (33), each complex Gaussian integral is pi/(a_i-a_j). Equation (37) needs pi^[r(d-r)] multiplying the same c_d,r. For d=2,r=1, c_2,1=1/pi and A=diag(a,b), the exact normalizer is (exp(sa)-exp(sb))/(s(a-b)); (37) is smaller by pi at leading order. This shifts the unspecified constant in (13), not spectral derivatives. Proposition 5.1 independently supplies the correct RDF normalization, so the main high-rate constant survives.

G3 | Local proof omission, Theorem 5.2, p. 8: localization plus concavity proves uniqueness of the maximizing radius in the localized annulus, whereas the statement calls b the unique positive solution of (21). To exclude other stationary roots, one additionally needs to use that lambda=r^2*kappa/[2*b(kappa)] is bounded on every bounded kappa interval, including its continuous positive limit at zero; thus large lambda forces kappa large and b near one. The positivity of b prime and the stated asymptotics supply this missing step. No contrary stationary branch or main-theorem counterexample was found.

assessments.summary: This exact nine-page v1 manuscript gives a credible complete classification of rank-below-7d/9 states admitting three-list discrimination for the fixed cyclic Weyl basis in d=3^k, k>=2. I found no counterexample to the algebraic claims. The most delicate universal step is the terse p-adic subgroup/radical analysis in Lemma 2; the finite replay supports but does not prove it for arbitrary k. Public-source checks confirmed that the cited state-classification, stabilizer-normal-form, Weyl-unitary, and discrete-Wigner antecedents exist and have the stated broad scope, not bibliographic priority for the new classification.
strengths: Lemma 1 states and proves an operational if-and-only-if factorization, with normalization and an explicit covariant POVM rather than only a necessary condition.
Lemma 3 uses positivity to constrain every summand simultaneously and converts the analytic rank cutoff into a finite affine-plane classification.
Theorem B distinguishes sparse-square count from list size and supplies explicit witnesses for l_min^exact(d,5d/9)=3 and l_min^exact(d,4d/9)=4.
The rerun programs use exact rational/Q(omega) arithmetic for the central finite geometry and matrix identities; no numerical rank threshold is used.
weaknesses: The proof that the radical is generated by q u and q v with the asserted order, and hence that every singular noncommuting trinomial has nullity at most two, is much terser than the rest of the paper.
The exhaustive label-pair computation is only for d=9; arbitrary k still rests entirely on the written p-adic normal-form proof.
Novelty is only boundedly searched, and the same-author predecessor cited as reference 1 was not among the supplied artifacts or located in the public checks.
The structural theorem is intentionally narrow: it does not address rank at or above 7d/9, approximation, or tensor-product qutrit Weyl bases.
potential_errors: Lemma 2's circle-intersection argument assumes the central-character pairs are distinct unit-modulus pairs and that the two circles cannot coincide. Nonzero c makes coincidence implausible, and I found no counterexample, but the manuscript does not spell out this exceptional-case exclusion algebraically.

The code verifies finite incidence and representative matrix identities, not the quantification over arbitrary complex coefficients in every 3^k dimension; passing it therefore cannot close a hypothetical gap in Lemma 2 or Lemma 3.
strong_novelty_candidates: The complete 150-relative-interior description of the low-rank three-list state set for the cyclic ternary Weyl basis.
The exact fixed-rank list-size nonmonotonicity 3,4,3,2 across ranks d/3,4d/9,5d/9,2d/3.
The uniqueness and minimum sparse-square length of every listed affine-line mixture.

correctness_confidence.basis: The quadratic reduction, inactive interpolation certificate, active positive dual certificate, two-port completion, and cubic inverse form a consistent proof chain; exact symbolic and Sturm reruns passed all reported identities, fixtures, and round trips.

rigor.basis: Both branches have explicit feasible constructions and lower certificates with positive weights, and the inverse is derived from the unique rank-one numerator family; the only substantial imported step is the classical degree-one Blaschke-Potapov/completion structure.

novelty.basis: The closed two-branch phase boundary, active certificate, compiler, and exact inverse appear specialized and nontrivial, but external priority is expressly not established and the public check was a bounded comparison against adjacent primary work.

significance.basis: The paper completely solves a sharply defined three-node, one-state, degree-at-most-one routing problem for every port count, but does not address more nodes, higher degree, loss, fixed phases, or physical component synthesis.

reproducibility.basis: Manifest-matched programs reran under Python 3.12 with SymPy 1.14 and mpmath 1.3: 9 symbolic groups, 2 rational fixtures, the radical obstruction fixture, 14 constructor cases, 74 exact Sturm cases, 4 inverse fixtures, 6 boundary cases, and 12 numerical round trips passed.

assessments.summary: This exact thirteen-page v1 manuscript presents a convincing complete minimax law for three prescribed routing nodes under a degree-at-most-one rational-inner and peak trace-delay constraint. The proof reduces every port count to two nonnegative quadratic intensities, obtains the inactive lower bound by Lagrange interpolation, identifies the loss of global residual positivity, and supplies a distinct active lower certificate with strictly positive endpoint weights. The explicit outer factor and 2x2 inner completion establish attainment, while the inverse problem is reduced to a single cubic with a monotonicity/Sturm-compatible uniqueness argument. I tested boundary and asymmetric fixtures through the supplied exact programs and found no counterexample. The result relies on classical degree-one Blaschke-Potapov and degree-preserving completion theory; the cited primary source supports that general structure, while the manuscript's special scalar construction makes most of the needed converse explicit.
strengths: The active branch is not inferred from a solver: equations (18)-(21) give a positive lower certificate valid for complex coefficients and arbitrary extra ports.
Section 6 provides a concrete two-port spectral factor and inner completion whose determinant has degree one and whose peak equals the prescribed cap.
Theorem 2 inverts the forward law globally, handles the T=0 and T=1 boundaries, and isolates at most one cubic root.
The exact rational active and boundary fixtures, symbolic identities, and independent Sturm checks substantially reduce the risk of a sign or branch-selection error.
weaknesses: The external novelty search is explicitly bounded, so the priority of the complete law and inverse remains unverified.
The initial reduction imports the classification of degree-one rational-inner matrices and degree-preserving completion rather than proving that general theorem from first principles.
The physical interpretation is limited to an abstract rational-inner routing model; no component, calibration, or loss realization is supplied.
The source/replay package referred to in Section 9 was not part of the PDF batch, although the later public-code batch supplied the relevant verification programs.
potential_errors: The universal N-port converse uses only the e2 intensity Q and aggregates all other outputs into P=H-Q. This is valid because the repeated e1-node constraints imply the necessary Q endpoint bounds and the constructed two-port solution attains them, but this reduction is easy to misread as preserving every original extra-port error equality.

The radical formula for the transition requires retaining the unsquared sign and larger root. The supplied symbolic and exact boundary checks support the manuscript's branch rule, but arbitrary floating-point use without those retained conditions could select a spurious root.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact positivity-driven phase boundary separating inactive and active minimax certificates.
The positive active-branch dual certificate together with an operational two-port compiler for all N>=2.
The exact error-target-to-minimum-delay inverse requiring at most one isolated cubic root.

correctness_confidence.basis: The weak-field moment selector, uniform strong-field Laplace expansion, exact eventual two-block optimization, Shannon-Gibbs converse, posterior self-consistency, and Selberg asymptotics form a coherent chain; exact constants and bounded diagnostics reran successfully.

rigor.basis: Appendices provide the delicate differentiated chart expansion and balanced fourth-moment calculation, while compact localization and strict transverse/radial Hessians supply eventual uniqueness; several uniformity steps remain concise rather than fully quantified with explicit constants.

novelty.basis: Optimizing the external spectrum at fixed finite dimension to force nonanalyticity, then using exact eventual two-block optimality to solve the unrestricted posterior-body RDF near zero distortion, is a strong novelty candidate relative to the checked antecedent scopes.

significance.basis: The work links finite-dimensional spectral optimization, matrix-Bingham asymptotics, and an exact high-fidelity classical rate-distortion frontier for every nontrivial rank, though the all-distortion curve and intermediate phases remain open.

reproducibility.basis: All four manifest-matched replay programs ran with Python 3.12, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0, SymPy 1.14, and Matplotlib 3.10.8, checking 1,558 weak/strong parameter pairs, d=5,r=2 quadrature, and 81 high-fidelity cases through d=18; the main uniform Laplace and global-optimality theorems are analytic and not certified by these scripts.

assessments.summary: This exact fourteen-page v1 manuscript makes a substantial and largely convincing connection between finite-dimensional matrix-Bingham spectral optimization and unrestricted high-fidelity rate-distortion on complex Grassmannians. The cubic Haar moment selects a positive one-spike weak-field orbit for 1<r<d/2, whereas a uniform differentiated Laplace expansion selects the rank-r two-block orbit exactly at sufficiently strong field; the mismatch forces nonanalyticity of the optimized envelope without overclaiming a first-order or unique transition. The information-theoretic half correctly reduces arbitrary standard-Borel memories to the posterior-density body, localizes the Shannon dual near its extreme orbit, and constructs a covariant Bingham channel whose posterior mean is the optimizing report. The Jacobi-Selberg calculation yields the stated sharp high-rate constant and complement transfer. I found no material contradiction. The existential thresholds and global analytic localization are not computationally reproduced, and the appendix's uniformity/quotient-Hessian steps deserve careful expert attention, but I did not identify a counterexample or a missing condition that invalidates a main result.
strengths: The paper separates weak-field, strong-field, and unknown intermediate regimes and does not infer the global nonanalytic point from the canonical-branch crossing.
Appendix A addresses the key need for two differentiated orders, including uniform exterior tails, Gaussian rescaling, and internal block collisions.
Theorem 6.1 proves unrestricted posterior-body attainment rather than restricting reproduction points to the source Grassmannian.
The covariant channel satisfies the Gibbs equality kernel and exact posterior-mean self-consistency, closing both converse and achievability.
The Selberg constant, complement scaling, d=5,r=2 normalizer, and high-rate tables were independently rerun from the supplied public programs.
weaknesses: The thresholds u*(d,r), lambda*(d,r), and D*(d,r) are existential; the theorem gives no effective interval for a concrete pair except diagnostic evidence.
The exact-eventual optimizer proof compresses the passage from spectral-coordinate Hessians to uniqueness modulo the full unitary orbit, especially at within-block eigenvalue collisions.
The public programs explicitly do not verify the uniform Laplace theorem, exact global optimizer, nonanalyticity, or unrestricted RDF converse; those remain dependent on the written analysis.
The bounded source check supports adjacency to matrix-Bingham, spherical-integral, Grassmann-quantization, and sphere-RDF work, but does not establish comprehensive bibliographic priority.
potential_errors: Theorem 4.3 requires uniform C2 control on a normal slice to the conjugacy orbit; Appendix A proves ordinary spectral derivative control, and the manuscript relies on unitary invariance to pass to the quotient. This appears sound but is the point most likely to hide a geometric regularity gap.

The bounded Monte Carlo spectral diagnostic at s=20 found sampled spectra with a larger estimated score than the canonical rank-two branch. This is not a contradiction because the theorem is only eventual and the estimate is a rare-event-sensitive finite-sample diagnostic, but it shows that the code does not locate the strong-field threshold.

Proposition 5.1's exponentially small remainder uses the special equal-rank complex Jacobi density with zero x-power. The d=5,r=2 quadrature and constants agree, but the general density normalization remains a mathematical input rather than a program-verified theorem.
strong_novelty_candidates: A fixed-finite-dimensional nonanalyticity forced by optimizing the external matrix-Bingham spectrum rather than by a thermodynamic limit.
Exact eventual rank-r two-block uniqueness obtained from a differentiated Grassmann Laplace expansion stable under internal block collisions.
The exact unrestricted high-fidelity rate-distortion parametrization with a posterior-mean-self-consistent covariant matrix-Bingham channel.
The explicit Jacobi-Selberg additive high-rate constant and complementary-rank distortion transfer.

correctness_confidence.basis: The Hilbert-function span argument, orbit-leverage inequality, three qubit branches, Segre count, and harmonic formulas are mutually consistent. The exact verifier ran successfully, although finite checks cannot validate the general algebraic and tester theorems.

rigor.basis: The main implications are proved and scope restrictions are unusually explicit. The Zariski-density assertions for physical projector orbits and the identification of the singular selective-phase image deserve fuller standalone justification.

novelty.basis: Primary-source checks confirm that unitary polynomial methods and general-tester dimension bounds are prior art. The exact Hilbert numerator, branch diagram, and all-k spectra appear plausible as a new synthesis, but the targeted search was not an exhaustive priority review.

significance.basis: Replacing the ambient polynomial dimension by a promise-variety Hilbert function gives a portable converse, and the fixed-angle and selective-phase examples demonstrate genuine exponent reductions. The results are bounds, not general attainability theorems.

reproducibility.basis: The standard-library exact verifier executed and passed its stated finite identities. However, the included figure and release-check scripts fail because the referenced paper and output trees are absent from this supplied public-code subset.

assessments.summary: This exact 14-page manuscript presents a coherent and apparently correct geometry-sensitive support theorem for forward unitary queries, extends it to compact transitive-orbit general testers, and derives detailed qubit, selective-phase, sphere, and circle formulas. I found no unresolved objection capable of invalidating a main claim. The main revisions needed are fuller justification of two closure assertions, tighter separation between verified novelty and synthesis, and a self-contained runnable code bundle.
strengths: Theorem 3.1 correctly identifies the annihilator of the Veronese span with the degree-k vanishing ideal, yielding the exact Hilbert function and a causal discrimination cap rather than only an ambient count.

Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.2 use constant orbit leverage correctly: averaging the pseudoinverse leverage gives rank D_k, and tester normalization applies to each repeated channel tuple and hence to the orbit average.
The fixed-angle qubit, Segre selective-phase, Funk-Hecke, purity, endpoint, and great-circle formulas agree algebraically; the supplied exact verifier passed all of its finite rational checks.
weaknesses: The proof of Theorem 6.1 states, rather than develops, why physical rank-one projectors are Zariski dense in the full Segre variety and why the exceptional d=2, c=-2 projection has closure P^2; these are central closure identifications.

Operational significance is limited by design: Hilbert rank is only a converse, and Theorem 7.1 is a scalability test for a fixed effective state family rather than a construction attaining the general-tester cap.

The public-code README describes a larger release tree than the files supplied here, so two advertised commands are not replayable from this batch without reconstructing missing directories and assets.
potential_errors: Equation (29)'s density argument is concise enough that a reader could miss the projective scaling step: a rank-one matrix with nonzero trace becomes an idempotent after scaling. The conclusion appears correct, but the omitted step should be explicit.

The novelty boundary relies partly on a targeted literature search and a cited 2026 ARR record. The checked primary sources establish important antecedents but do not prove priority for the exact combined theorem package.
strong_novelty_candidates: The promise-sensitive replacement of the ambient general-tester numerator by the exact Hilbert rank for compact transitive unitary orbits is a strong candidate, subject to a broader priority search.
The complete branch-resolved fixed-angle support laws together with the all-k sphere and circle spectra form a specific, technically substantial candidate contribution.

correctness_confidence.basis: The squared-harmonic coefficient, negative Laplacian, criticality guard, Schur-lemma upgrade, Jacobi closure, and weak-field sign logic check out. Independent finite sign and torus diagnostics passed; the bundled symbolic replay itself could not run unchanged.

rigor.basis: The paper repairs the criticality gap explicitly and separates local from global conclusions. Some central representation facts for the three half-Grassmannians and invariant covariance formulas are asserted compactly and should be proved or cited in greater detail.

novelty.basis: The harmonic positivity and Jacobi machinery are established and acknowledged. The all-field Morse-Bott application and the 2r/3 metastability threshold are credible novelty candidates, but the search checked only selected primary sources and not the full specialized literature.

significance.basis: The no-spinodal result and exact local phase classification materially constrain the motivating optimization problem, but the manuscript expressly leaves global spectral ordering and the full rate-distortion consequence unresolved.

reproducibility.basis: A script and frozen output are supplied, but the README gives no dependency specification and execution failed because sympy and mpmath were unavailable. Independent standard-library/SciPy checks covered 435 threshold cases, ten boundary cases, and the torus derivative only.

assessments.summary: This exact 11-page manuscript gives a sound local-stability framework: harmonic positivity supplies a strict Laplacian trace, an explicit criticality condition prevents a false irreducibility shortcut, and isotropy converts the trace into a Morse-Bott maximum. The half-Grassmann application and complex Jacobi weak-field threshold appear mathematically consistent. No main claim was refuted, but key representation assertions and replay dependencies need strengthening, and the global optimization problem remains deliberately open.
strengths: Lemma 2.1 turns the orbit coefficient into a sum of squared harmonic means; Proposition 2.2 then gives a genuinely sign-definite spherical-Laplacian identity for strictly positive kernel coefficients.
Theorem 3.2 includes the necessary criticality hypothesis, and Remark 3.3 supplies a concrete antipodal torus orbit showing that irreducible normal isotropy alone does not force criticality.

The Jacobi generator identities reduce both block-splitting Hessians to scalar differential operators, and the moment signs consistently yield the k=2r/3 weak-field boundary and its quartic degeneracy.
weaknesses: The half-Grassmann proof compresses the normal-space decomposition, real irreducibility for R, C, and H, and the block-exchange action into one paragraph; these facts carry the all-field application and merit explicit lemmas or precise references.
Equations (6.1)-(6.3) invoke an invariant covariance formula without deriving its normalization fully, making the exact Hessian eigenvalues harder to audit than the surrounding algebra.

The coefficient-tail theorem proves only eventual coefficientwise sign for each fixed (r,k); it does not close the remaining finite gate or establish an all-field sign for unbalanced branches, a limitation the paper does acknowledge.
potential_errors: The bundled replay was not executable from the supplied instructions because sympy and mpmath were undeclared and absent. Its stored JSON output was therefore not counted as an execution result.

The continuity argument in Corollary 3.4 is plausible, but a precise uniform bound on third derivatives over the chosen tube and compact field interval would make the claimed common tubular neighborhood fully explicit.
strong_novelty_candidates: The criticality-guarded all-field Morse-Bott criterion for antipodal homogeneous source orbits is a concise candidate contribution built from classical harmonic ingredients.
The exact complex half-Grassmann weak-field metastability threshold k=2r/3, including the sixth-moment boundary, is a strong specific candidate if priority survives a specialist search.

correctness_confidence.basis: The support inequalities, matroid-union rank collapse, process compression, laminar decision-tree reduction, dense-coding SDP, and explicit attainability and insufficiency examples are internally consistent. All four supplied replay programs executed successfully.

rigor.basis: The main theorem is short and complete, and limitations are carefully separated from feasibility. The adaptive quantum-to-classical reduction and the intermediate-spectrum list optimum are convincing but sufficiently compressed that fuller channel-state bookkeeping would improve auditability.

novelty.basis: Rado-Edmonds theory, state exclusion, tester normalization, and the dense-coding spectrum law are established and credited. The union-polytope inclusion theorem and exact architecture applications look like plausible new combinations, but priority was not exhaustively established.

significance.basis: The all-subset Bayes bound retains labeled support congestion and applies to arbitrary priors, mixed states, soft lists, and tester compression. Exact examples sharply distinguish combinatorial obstruction from physical attainability and isolate feedback resources.

reproducibility.basis: All four standard-library programs ran cleanly, covering 240 union-rank cases, exact simplex and qubit certificates, 70 laminar phase cases, UEB fibres, Schmidt caps, and wiring values. The programs appropriately describe themselves as finite checks, not proofs.

assessments.summary: This exact 20-page manuscript proves a clean and useful matroid-union outer bound for quantum list discrimination and transports it correctly through fixed tester normalizations. The arbitrary-prior formula, soft-list extension, exact laminar adaptive/parallel phase, simplex attainment, and qubit nonsufficiency certificate make the boundary of the theorem unusually clear. I found no unresolved material objection. Minor revision should expand two compressed operational proofs and temper novelty claims to the limits of the literature search.
strengths: Theorem 4.1 correctly combines the operator inequality rho_i <= P_A, the per-outcome reward budget, and singleton bounds to obtain exactly the independence polytope of the ell-fold Rado-matroid union.
Lemma 5.1 preserves all tester probabilities under Moore-Penrose compression, while Theorem 5.2 correctly uses a common linear map to obtain a tester-independent but explicitly coarser support cap.
The regular-simplex root-frame POVM and the three-qubit primal-dual exclusion certificate rigorously show both exact attainment and failure of support sufficiency within transparent finite examples.

The laminar-channel theorem distinguishes parallel cells from adaptive decision-tree leaves and proves matching constructions against the stated entangled-parallel and quantum-memory strategy classes.
weaknesses: The adaptive part of Theorem 6.1 relies on a concise genie-flag induction; writing the conditional memory state and its label-independence invariant explicitly would make the reduction robust to instrument and transcript conventions.

The D=4 rank-two list optimum in Equation (36) is sketched through sector pinching and a covariant dual; the full normalization across four shift sectors is not displayed in the manuscript even though the fixture checks the value.

Several potentially new components are direct combinations of classical matroid union, support domination, and standard tester compression, so the contribution is substantial synthesis rather than a new foundational discrimination formalism.
potential_errors: Corollary 8.1 refers to Theorem 4.2, although the relevant arbitrary-prior statement is Corollary 4.2; this appears to be a cross-reference error rather than a mathematical flaw.

The phrase 'complete input-dependent family' in the abstract could be read broadly, while Theorem 6.2 concerns one specially constructed laminar family with uniform priors and power-of-two list sizes.
strong_novelty_candidates: Embedding the entire inclusion-probability vector into the ell-fold Rado-matroid independence polytope, with arbitrary priors and soft reward budgets, is the clearest general candidate contribution.
The exact all-depth laminar channel phase against arbitrary entangled parallel inputs and adaptive quantum memories is a concrete architecture-sensitive novelty candidate.
The paired simplex-attainment and hemisphere-obstruction examples give a sharp, reusable account of where the support obstruction is exact and where quantum geometry remains decisive.

correctness_confidence.basis: Theorems 3.1, 5.1 and 6.1 have valid annihilator/closure arguments; the harmonic spectrum, purity and tightness obstruction agree with exact replay. Direct rational feature ranks independently match all three qubit branches for k=1..4. No main-result counterexample was found.

rigor.basis: The forward-query model and nonattainment qualifications are precise. Theorem 4.2 is valid, but its advertised separation from the arbitrary-family causal bound overlooks canonical tester compression. Lemma 4.1 should explicitly require a unitary linear action on Choi vectors.

novelty.basis: The promise-specific Hilbert laws and combined all-k spectra are credible incremental contributions. Ref. [3], Appendix F, already supplies orbit domination; refs. [2] and [9] establish polynomial/rank antecedents. Transitivity is unnecessary for the probability cap. Priority over self-cited ref. [11] was not independently established.

significance.basis: The exact Segre exponent 2d-2 and the quadratic-versus-linear support/participation contrast are useful structural results. They give necessary query counts, not matching generic discrimination algorithms, robustness guarantees or a field-wide complexity breakthrough.

reproducibility.basis: The supplied standard-library verifier ran successfully: qubit k=1..12, qudit d=2..8 and k=1..8, and tightness k=2..49. Independent exact evaluation ranks also passed. These are finite algebra checks; no general-tester SDP, manuscript rebuild or formal proof was executed.

assessments.summary: This exact 14-page v1 supports its principal Hilbert-rank, singular-branch, Segre and harmonic-spectrum conclusions. The annihilator proof and Bell exposure are sound, and the three-sector tightness obstruction survives exact checks. The contribution is a useful synthesis of classical geometry and discrimination bounds, rather than a new polynomial method or tester theory. A substantive presentation issue is that canonical tester compression already extends the Hilbert probability bound to arbitrary families, so orbit transitivity is not needed for the advertised upgrade. I found no unresolved objection invalidating the stated main theorems; minor revision is appropriate for this scope/novelty distinction and replay documentation. The score reflects strong incremental research, with incomplete priority verification and no claim of operational saturation.
strengths: Theorem 3.1, p.4: the annihilator of span{U^tensor k} is exactly I(X)_k; quotient dimension therefore gives H_X(k). Vectorized parallel Bell outputs expose that entire span, so the maximum causal-support assertion is an equality, not merely an upper bound.

Theorems 5.1 and 6.1, pp.6-8: the quadric, traceless projective plane and central point give distinct correct branches. For selective-phase qudits L_c(X)=Tr(X)I+cX has eigenvalues c+d and c; the physical exceptional singularity c=-d occurs only at d=2,c=-2. The Segre Hilbert count and two-query defect follow.

Theorem 8.1 and Proposition 8.2, pp.9-10: the zonal kernel (a+b n.m)^k gives the stated Legendre moments and multiplicities. Integrating its square yields the purity formula and linear participation dimension for a fixed interior angle; endpoint parity and rank losses are consistent.

Theorem 9.1, p.11: equal top harmonic eigenvalues force a/b=1/(2k+1), after which the third-sector ratio is k(2k+3)/(2k+1)>1. Sector-trace invariance also justifies the positive-reweighting obstruction; this is stronger than checking only uniform designs.

Theorem 7.1, p.9, correctly separates rank from attainable success through positive scalability KCK=K. The manuscript also correctly warns that antipodal traceless axes are identical channels and that necessary query bounds do not construct attaining protocols.
weaknesses: Sections 4 and 12, pp.5,13: the causal-versus-GEN boundary is unnecessarily restrictive. Put v_i=|U_i>>^tensor k and w_i=W^(1/2)v_i. Equation (5) makes w_i unit vectors; W^(-1/2)T_iW^(-1/2) is a POVM on supp W. Their span has dimension at most H_X(k), giving the same H_X(k)/M bound for arbitrary families. This weakens the claimed special role of orbit leverage but does not falsify Theorem 4.2.

Novelty boundary, pp.2-3,13-14: Bavaresco-Murao-Quintino Theorem 5 and Appendix F already contain the ambient cap and group-average domination (https://arxiv.org/html/2105.13369v3). The credible additional content is the exact promise geometry and spectra. The special 24-echo predecessor [11] was not retrieved, so its overlap and priority remain unverified.

Section 12 calls the verifier range configurable, but the supplied main() hard-codes its ranges and has no command-line range option. Its leverage check sums harmonic multiplicities rather than constructing an orbit average or a tester. This is narrower evidence than a direct operational verification.

The supplied reproducibility README refers to verification/ and paper/ layouts and manuscript sources absent from this batch. The exact checker runs directly, but the release rebuild and package_release.py --check were not reproduced. No failure of the supplied canonical PDF hash is implied.

Sections 11-12: exact rank is discontinuous at singular promises and does not quantify noisy discrimination or the attainable success of generic finite subsets. The manuscript acknowledges these limits; they cap the practical significance of the asymptotic support exponent.
potential_errors: Lemma 4.1, p.5: transitivity of an abstract action on a set of unitaries alone does not imply a unitary representation on their Choi-vector span. State the linear/unitary covariance assumption used in the proof. The conjugation actions in all concrete applications satisfy it, so this is a formulation issue rather than a demonstrated application failure.

Section 11, p.13: the necessary query scale is said to drop when the support exponent decreases. For fixed d and large M, M^(1/(2d-2)) grows faster than the ambient M^(1/(d^2-1)); the promise strengthens (raises) the necessary query count. The displayed formula is correct.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 6.1: the projectively transformed Segre description supplies an exact all-dimension, all-query support law with the physically constrained singular branch; this is more specific than the classical Hilbert-function identity.

The combined Theorems 8.1, 9.1 and 10.1: exact sphere/circle spectra, endpoint cascades and the all-k Bell-tightness obstruction form a potentially useful package for constrained oracle discrimination. Priority is a candidate assessment, not an exhaustive literature conclusion.

correctness_confidence.basis: The squared orbital coefficients, criticality guard and normal-isotropy argument support Theorems 3.2 and 4.1. Exact replay verifies the moment/Taylor signs; independent Jacobi-density integration at r=3,k=2 confirms the degenerate negative quartic coefficient. No main theorem was refuted.

rigor.basis: Criticality and vanishing mixed Hessian entries are explicitly proved before the Laplacian trace is promoted to definiteness. The two block modules exhaust the normal space. The finite-tail gate is honestly left open; Section 8 needs a minor correction for its identically zero constant coefficient.

novelty.basis: The all-field normal-Hessian conclusion across R,C,H and the k=2r/3 metastability boundary are credible new combinations of classical harmonic positivity and Jacobi moments. Selected primary-source checks support the classical antecedents, but priority against the two self-cited predecessor papers and the whole stability literature was not established.

significance.basis: All-field balanced local rigidity and explicit weak-field stable unbalanced strata materially constrain possible spectral phase arguments. The result remains local: it neither orders all external spectra nor solves the global rate-distortion problem. The 4.6 score reflects that useful but bounded advance.

reproducibility.basis: The supplied replay passed after installing SymPy 1.14.0 and mpmath 1.3.0 locally: symbolic moments/signs, 55 integer cases, 60 numerical Bessel cases and the torus diagnostic. Independent polynomial integration and generator calculations also passed. No stored certificate was counted as execution; no Lean proof is supplied.

assessments.summary: The exact 11-page v1 gives a convincing local stability theorem, with a necessary criticality hypothesis that the half-Grassmann applications actually satisfy. Its Jacobi Hessian reduction and weak-field threshold survive symbolic replay and independent exact checks, including the sixth-moment boundary. The near-balanced metastable branches correctly invalidate an indiscriminate saddle shortcut, while the balanced branch remains locally stable at every positive field. I found no unresolved objection capable of invalidating these main claims. Minor revision should clarify the zero constant coefficient in Section 8, the field-order convention for the Hessian signs, and reproducibility details. Global spectral optimality, all-distortion rate-distortion and exhaustive novelty are not established and receive no credit as proved results.
strengths: Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 2.2, p.3: averaging the addition theorem over both source-orbit variables produces squared harmonic means. A proper compact orbit cannot carry ambient uniform measure, so a nonconstant mode is present; positive exponential coefficients make the spherical Laplacian strictly negative for every t>0.

Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp.3-4: the gradient lies in the normal isotropy fixed space. At a critical orbit differentiating invariance annihilates tangent and mixed Hessian terms; self-adjoint equivariance and the stated block symmetry then turn the negative trace into strict normal definiteness. The torus example correctly shows why orbit constancy alone is insufficient.

Theorem 4.1, pp.4-5: the real dimensions, two traceless diagonal normal modules and off-diagonal tangent directions are consistent. Block-swap composed with sign reversal fixes the balanced point and exchanges modules, while the stabilizer has no fixed traceless vector. This supplies the missing hypotheses over R,C,H for r>=2.

Lemma 5.2 and Theorem 6.1, pp.6-7: direct symbolic differentiation of the stated Jacobi generator at k=1..4 confirmed LY=-2rY and LS=k(2r-k)/2+2Y^2-4rS. The posterior covariance and spherical multiplier combine with the displayed denominators to give the two scalar Hessian operators; k=1 is correctly excluded from positive-block splitting.

Theorem 7.1 and Appendix A, pp.7-10: exact replay confirms both quadratic coefficients and the sixth-moment boundary. Independent integration of x(1-x)y(1-y)(x-y)^2 at r=3,k=2 gives mu2=2/35, mu4=1/105, mu6=4/1617, [u^2]Hminus=0 and [u^4]Hminus=-1/16170. The boundary instability therefore survives a check independent of the Schur expansion.

Proposition 8.1 and Section 9, pp.8-9: the pointwise S<=k/4-Y^2/k inequality yields the moment-ratio tail bound. The paper does not promote the finite remaining gate into an all-rank theorem and does not infer global optimality from the absence of a balanced spinodal.
weaknesses: Theorem 3.2 is structurally persuasive but the applications compress several representation-theory facts into one paragraph. Explicit stabilizer groups and normal-module dimensions, especially for quaternionic r=2, would make the real irreducibility and zero-fixed-vector checks easier to audit without changing the proof mechanism.

Section 8 proves eventual negativity of coefficients, not negativity of Hminus at every field for every multiplicity. For 2r/3<k<r the positive low-degree term is real, consistent with metastability. Any later global sign or phase claim still requires the stated low-degree/value-comparison work.

Section 10: the Bessel replay checks positivity of isolated formula terms on 60 cases; it does not compute orbital coefficients q_l or a full Grassmann Hessian. The ambient-dimension dictionary restates expressions rather than independently counting modules. These are limited diagnostics despite a successful run.

The replay depends on SymPy and mpmath, while the supplied README says only Python 3 and contains no pinned dependency file. The first execution stopped at missing mpmath; installing local dependencies resolved it. The supplied Lean README explicitly contains no formalization.

Selected source inspection confirms the Jacobi-density antecedent in Dumitriu-Edelman, Eq. (5), and the trace-transform framework in Forrester-Kumar (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.00787). The claimed distinction from self-cited refs. [5]-[6] and all citation-specific priority assertions remain unverified; no comprehensive novelty finding is warranted.
potential_errors: Section 8, Eq. (8.1), p.8: literal strict coefficientwise negativity cannot include j=0. From mu2=km/[4(n^2-1)] and A=n(nm-1)/k, (1+A)mu2=m^2/4, so Hminus(0)=0 and the displayed strict ratio becomes equality at j=0. Restrict the strict discussion to nonconstant even coefficients. The tail proposition and main stability results are unaffected.

Theorem 7.1(ii), pp.7-8: order u^4 is the order of Hminus, or equivalently of Hess(F_s)/s^2 up to its analytic positive factor. The actual Hessian of F_s includes s^2 and first becomes nonzero at order s^6 on the degenerate boundary. Specify this normalization to avoid an incorrect reading of the claimed onset order.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 4.1: all-positive-field constrained local maximality of the balanced half-Grassmann field over all three division algebras, obtained through harmonic positivity and a critical normal-isotropy criterion.

Theorem 7.1: exact weak-field stable unbalanced multiplicities 2r/3<k<r, together with the negative sixth-moment boundary coefficient, offer a concrete obstruction to saddle-only global proofs. These local results are stronger novelty candidates than the classical matrix-beta or Jacobi identities themselves.

correctness_confidence.basis: The closed union-rank substitution and all-subset support inequality are sound. Canonical compression handles singular tester normalizations correctly. The laminar flag reduction and the stated restricted Weyl wirings have matching constructions. Supplied tests and an independent exact matrix certificate support the concrete optima.

Zero priors, soft rewards, core tails and compression losses are treated explicitly. Computational claims in Sections 11 and 13 exceed what the multitime replay actually checks.

Primary checks confirm the dense-coding spectrum law and the stronger projector obstruction; the self-cited one-label predecessor was not checked for overlap.

significance.basis: The bound improves total dimension for congested high-prior clusters and gives useful exact attainment examples. It can be vacuous for full-rank mixed states and is not a complete feasibility test. The architecture separations rely on deliberately classical dephasing channels or tightly restricted memory resources.

reproducibility.basis: All four supplied scripts pass, including 240 rank/subset/budget cases and 70 laminar cases. However verify_multitime_ueb.py uses float square roots and formula comparisons, not exact frame spectra or PSD tests. assessments.summary: The exact 20-page v1 establishes a sound support-based Bayesian list hierarchy by combining elementary quantum inequalities with classical Rado-Edmonds theory. Its process compression, laminar-channel phase, simplex POVM and qubit exclusion certificate are consistent with their proofs and the executed checks. The work is substantive but primarily a synthesis: dense-coding optimality and the basic exclusion/feedback mechanisms are prior art, and the support cap is not generally attainable. No unresolved main-claim-invalidating objection was found. Minor revision is warranted because the manuscript overstates the exactness and scope of its multitime replay and should sharpen several novelty and resource qualifications. The score credits the all-subset formulation and exact examples without crediting a general solution of quantum list discrimination.
strengths: Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 4.1, pp.4-5: substituting the Rado rank into Edmonds union and writing B=C disjoint-union F leaves the nonnegative term (ell-1)|F|. Combining rho_i<=P_A with the per-outcome budget and s_i<=1 therefore gives exactly the stated union-rank inequalities, including mixed supports and soft rewards.

Proposition 4.3, p.6: summation by parts over sorted priors makes each weighted prefix deficit nonnegative. Equality is consequently equivalent to saturation only at strict prior drops; zero priors and ties cause no hidden extra equality conditions.

Lemma 5.1, Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 5.3, pp.6-8: restricting inverse square roots to supp T correctly produces a POVM and normalized effective states. Common congruence cannot raise any support-sum rank. The positive core argument remains valid for subnormalized cores, and the separate tail suprema are explicitly distinguished.

Theorems 6.1-6.2, pp.8-10: common input dephasing permits a label-independent flag decomposition, including reference systems. Conditional adaptive memory contains no information beyond the flagged transcript. Laminar cells give q+1 parallel classes and feedback gives at most 2^q leaves; the breadth-first and prefix-following constructions attain both bounds for ell=2^s.

Theorems 7.1-7.2, pp.10-12: the complete-error-basis twirl gives S=D I tensor rho_R and a constant PGM overlap, with a matching dual. The Weyl fibre sizes and terminal support dimensions correctly give the stated SER0/PAR0/PARBell laws under their explicit restrictions.

Theorem 9.2 and Proposition 10.1, pp.14-16: the root-frame effects sum to identity and annihilate every omitted simplex vertex. The qubit circumcenter has radius 1/sqrt(3), positive barycentric weights and matching exclusion primal/dual cost. These examples establish both attainment and genuine insufficiency of full union rank.
weaknesses: Sections 11 and 13, pp.16-18, describe exact rational/algebraic checks of complete-unitary-basis frame spectra and a fixed-probe certificate. The supplied verify_multitime_ueb.py constructs neither frame matrices nor POVM effects/dual slacks; it uses floating square roots, tolerances and equality of formula values. The successful replay is much weaker evidence than that description.

Section 11 describes 240 small subspace instances, but verify_list_matroid_union.py uses only three support fixtures and counts their subset/list-budget combinations. The number 240 is correct as a case count, not as the number of independently varied subspace families.

Section 7 and related work: Feng-Duan-Ji already derive and attain the approximate dense-coding formula (Eq. (17), https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0604149). The paper acknowledges this; the process-list translation and restricted wiring consequences should carry the novelty claim, rather than the spectrum formula itself.

Section 8: the projector obstruction of Stratton-Hsieh-Skrzypczyk can be stronger than the union density threshold, as the paper acknowledges. In the qubit example the largest eigenvalue of sum rho_i is (15+sqrt(153))/10>2, already excluding a perfect two-list POVM. The new value calculation is useful, but the impossibility is not a new feasibility criterion.

Sections 5 and 13: full-rank perturbations can trivialize support bounds; selecting useful positive cores remains an extra optimization. The 81/100 cap is not shown attainable, and no optimal algorithm for general priors, noise or unrestricted process architectures is proved.

Priority and packaging: the one-label predecessor [3] was not retrieved, so incremental overlap remains unverified. The supplied batch contains the replay scripts but not the LaTeX/bibliography package advertised on p.18; a manuscript rebuild was therefore not performed. No stored or author-provided report was treated as independent evidence.
potential_errors: Section 7, p.12: the D=4 rank-two fixture is described as an intermediate entanglement spectrum, although its nonzero Schmidt spectrum is flat (1/2,1/2). It demonstrates nonsaturation of the coarse list cap at intermediate Schmidt rank, not a nonflat-spectrum effect. The numerical value (2+sqrt(2))/4 itself is correct.

Section 6, p.9: the insertion proof for q+1 laminar cells needs the inclusion-compatible order to put containing sets before contained sets; an arbitrary insertion can meet several existing cells. A parent-first order exists and makes the proof work, so this is a minor clarification, not a counterexample to the phase law.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorems 4.1-4.3 and Corollary 5.3: inclusion vectors for arbitrary-prior mixed-state soft-list decisions lie in a single exact union-matroid independence polytope, with a prefix equality audit and a positive-core tail extension. The contribution is the operational synthesis, not new matroid theory.

Theorem 6.2: the exact all-depth list/feedback phase against arbitrary parallel entanglement and adaptive quantum memories is a clear, fully bounded application. It remains a classical-query mechanism embedded in channels, as explicitly stated.

The juxtaposition of an all-size simplex attainment family, the exact hemisphere optimum and the intermediate-rank list-cap failure gives concrete boundaries between support combinatorics and POVM geometry; priority for the package remains provisional.

The boundary-fibre and disk-collapse arguments are useful, but the radial-cut disintegration still needs an explicit constrained coordinate proof. The universal gap statement also needs to exclude the trivial compact connected group. The supplied batch does not support independent reproduction of the advertised Lean builds. These unresolved issues prevent an accept recommendation; neither the numerical replay nor this assessment verifies the claimed formal compilation. The result is a modest boundary-sector assembly, not a Millennium-problem advance.
strengths: Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 3.8, pp. 3 and 6: Schur averaging contributes 1/d_lambda, cancelling the heat-kernel dimension. The PDF correctly includes the complex conjugate of chi_lambda(h); this matters for general compact groups.

Lemmas 3.2-3.3, pp. 3-4: the adjacent eliminated-coordinate change is Haar preserving, including subdivision of the boundary edge used to impose holonomy. Face subdivision follows from the normalized heat convolution identity.

Lemmas 3.4-3.5, pp. 4-5: insertion of a transverse PL arc uses the analytically covered edge/face moves. The disk proof counts |E|-|V|+1=|F| and eliminates a dual tree from its leaves, preserving total area.

Propositions 4.1-4.2 and Theorem 5.1, pp. 7-8: orthogonal conjugation averaging, Parseval and the semigroup square establish the class-sector contraction, reflected positivity and complete minimum-Casimir equality space.

Corollary 5.3 and Proposition 5.4, pp. 8-9: n(n+2)/4 has unique positive minimum 3/4 at n=1; the quotient retains even labels and first reaches 2 at n=2. Product eigenvalues add, giving the stated minimum-sector rule.

Section 7 numerical replay actually completed: endpoint error 0, Gram error 2.709e-14, multiplier error 6.939e-18, sharp-mode index 1, and reflected form 1.7639228388840671. These are finite floating diagnostics only.
weaknesses: Sections 1 and 8: much of the headline theorem is an explicit assembly of known facts. Section 6 and Appendix C describe complete 2817-job and 3097-job builds. Those are manuscript claims, not this referee's executions; the batch contains only the scalar satellite modules and package pins, not the required mathematical library.
Section 7 tests the advertised formulas after assuming their spectral form; it does not test an arbitrary annular edge integral, a radial-cut measure identity, or the infinite-dimensional completion.

Appendix A: strict positivity follows because every spectral weight is positive, but density alone would only preserve nonnegativity. An explicit all-L2 Parseval sentence would make this last inference precise.
potential_errors: Theorem 1.1 and Section 5 include G={1}, a compact connected zero-dimensional Lie group. Its nontrivial dual is empty, so min_{lambda!=1} c_lambda is undefined; the mean-zero Hilbert space is zero and its spectrum is empty. The positive-gap and saturating-irrep assertions require nontrivial G.

Lemma 3.6, pp. 5-6: a spanning-tree vertex gauge sends a marked boundary holonomy h to k^{-1}hk. For example, noncommuting SU(2) choices can send h to -h. Holding h fixed therefore requires endpoint constraints or explicit tracking of this conjugation; invariance of unconstrained Haar factors alone is insufficient.

The proposed concrete SU(2) formal endpoints could be a reproducible formalization contribution. Only the scalar source was inspectable here; originality and compilation of the larger development remain unverified.

The proof needs a measure-preserving coordinate map that retains both marked boundary constraints and tracks identified copies of the cut. Conditioning on g,h and relative transport does not automatically give the single-holonomy disk fibre of Lemma 3.5. This is an unresolved proof-interface objection, not a counterexample to the classical cylinder formula.

Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 5.1 need a nontrivial-group hypothesis or a separate convention and statement for G={1}; as written the minimum Casimir and the claimed positive spectral gap are not defined in that allowed case.

The machine-checked claims in Section 6 cannot be independently checked from this supplied payload. Appendix C's reproduce.ps1, lean-2d-yang-mills.bundle and imported endpoint sources are missing. Provide the exact executable source payload before treating the advertised formal frontier as verified evidence.

Proposition 3.1, p. 3: direct endpoint subtraction gives the eleven edges and component sizes 7,4,2. The standalone graph/parity function executed successfully; the n=4 coefficient uses log(2), as required by the von Mangoldt weight.

Theorem 4.1, p. 4: the Markov identity gives the squared remainder with the stated x^(2m+1) factor, and Jacobi block inversion gives positive increments. Independent 80-decimal diagnostics for m=1,2,3,5 agree with the remainder, resolvent and endpoint formulas to about 1e-80.

Corollary 4.2, p. 4: monotone form convergence is supplemented by the common compact control A2 with H_n tending to infinity. This supports convergence of fixed eigenvalues and finite detection of strictly positive, but not zero-ground, cases.

Theorem 5.1 and Lemmas 5.2-5.3, pp. 5-6: inverse antitonicity avoids assuming invariant degree subspaces; congruence transport and the coupling-norm charge are logically appropriate. Rational arithmetic on Table 3 reproduces both conservative public floors, conditional on the input bounds.

correctness_confidence.basis: Theorems 1.2-1.3 follow from explicit jet separators, tangent escape and the minimal-degree radical argument. Proposition 7.1 and the characteristic-zero construction in Theorem 1.6 survive individual checking. No material counterexample or proof gap was found.

Product jet separation is related to established Terracini results. Priority is only selectively checked; the cited working notes and companion paper were not used.
