Independent finite-field searches found no bound violation. The code does not certify global smoothness or universal theorems.

assessments.summary: This exact 10-page manuscript establishes a modest but substantive geometric result within its stated scope. The characteristic-free kernel and escape arguments, including the Frobenius/radical step, are sound on inspection. The independent growing bound and factorized-polarization criterion follow with the correct quantifiers, and the complex hypersurface construction supplies sharp exceptional-branch examples without claiming global optimality. All six supplied exact fixtures ran successfully; an additional finite-field search found no counterexample in its explicitly limited cases. I found no unresolved material objection. Novelty remains a qualified candidate rather than an exhaustively established priority claim, and the existential Bertini step was assessed mathematically rather than by a computed globally smooth equation.
strengths: Lemma 2.1, pp. 3-4: equality of value and double-point annihilators is exactly equivalent to tangent absorption. This uses the full H^m section space and does not confuse an ordinary Terracini rank defect with equality of the two ranks.

Lemmas 3.1-3.2, pp. 4-5: squared pair separators kill first jets at unwanted points while a local unit preserves surjectivity at the target. The degree counts 2r-1 and 2r are correct, including the mixed simple point.

Lemmas 4.1-4.2 and Theorem 1.2, pp. 5-6: lambda*mu^(m-1) detects a tangent escaping the support span without a factor m. Repeated escape gives d+2 independent supports; failure at d+1 forces one common affine tangent W.

Lemma 5.1, p. 6: after raising a minimal-degree vanishing form to degree m by a local unit, absorption forces all its first partials to vanish on Z. A nonzero partial contradicts minimality; otherwise perfectness gives a pth root and radicality gives the lower-degree contradiction.

Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 7.1, pp. 6-7: the parity cases give the printed J(d,m), including the +1 for even m. A product of two point separators vanishes to order two at p but not at q, proving Gauss injectivity for the complete H-system.

Proposition 8.3 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 7-8: finite triple-jet interpolation fixes nodes, Bertini supplies smoothness away from them, G(p_i)!=0 makes F=f+x0*G smooth at them, and e>m with vanishing H^1 identifies the complete O_X(m) system. Simplex unisolvence then makes the N value vectors span every required tangent.

Actual replay results: simplex value/jet ranks are 10 and 20; the triple-jet rank is 18; sampled quadratic-Veronese tangent ranks are 3 with pair-union rank 5; the incomplete O(5) endpoint tangent union has rank 2. All six supplied fixtures pass.

Independent modular-rank search tested all 212 nonempty subsets in P1(F2), P1(F3), P1(F5), P2(F2), at degrees 3,3,4,3 respectively. No claimed-bound violation was found; these finitely many projective-space cases do not prove the general theorem.
weaknesses: Theorem 1.6 is existential and uses degree e=3*binomial(d+m,d); no effective smooth equation, optimized hypersurface degree or classification of equality configurations is provided. These are scope limits, not failures of the stated theorem.

The growing bound J(d,m) is not claimed sharp. For large m and d>1 it grows only linearly, while the exceptional branch is binomial. The paper does not determine the exact global floor in positive characteristic.

Novelty comparison is selective. Ballico-Chiantini already provide product criteria for independent first jets (https://arxiv.org/html/2011.13189v1, Section 3); the present contribution must be assessed through the additional absorption constraint and characteristic-free deductions.

The supplied Frobenius fixture only reduces derivative coefficients modulo 2,3,5, and the incomplete-subsystem fixture hard-codes endpoint tangent rows. Their PASS statuses do not prove radical descent or global injectivity; those steps were instead checked in the written arguments.

The cited companion global-floor theorem and working-note priority claims were not independently assessed. They are not dependencies of the proofs of Theorems 1.2, 1.3 or 1.6, so this limitation does not leave a material gap in those results.
strong_novelty_candidates: Lemma 5.1 combined with Theorem 1.2: radical descent in the all-zero-partials case gives a clean characteristic-free unisolvence mechanism for reduced absorbing sets in a common original Gauss fibre.

Theorem 1.6: prescribed nodal hyperplane sections together with simplex unisolvence realize exactly binomial(d+m,d) absorbing supports on smooth complex hypersurfaces for every d>=2,m>=3. This is a credible specialized construction, with priority not exhaustively established.
Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 provide complementary refinements: a degree-growing jet-block floor and a simple factorization criterion excluding the exceptional branch in complete embeddings.

correctness_confidence.basis: Theorem 1.1's chain is mathematically coherent: conditional Haar fibers, subdivision identities, disk collapse, orbital averaging, and Peter-Weyl diagonalization yield the stated kernel and sharp Casimir gap. No counterexample was found within the regular finite, compact connected scope.

rigor.basis: Lemmas 3.2-3.5 close several normalization and topology interfaces explicitly, and Theorems 3.8 and 5.1 justify convergence and equality cases. Lemma 3.6 remains compressed at the general combinatorial-coordinate level, and 'regular cellulation' is not formally defined.

significance.basis: The exact class-sector gap and cellulation-independent finite reduction are useful clarifications for solvable two-dimensional Yang-Mills. The result is deliberately limited to boundary class functions and does not address continuum reconstruction, bulk observables, or four-dimensional mass gap.

assessments.summary: This nine-page paper is concise and mostly convincing. The defect-one Fermat perturbation has the stated Milnor/Tjurina values under d(s-1)>s+1, and the global construction's separator jets, Bertini/incidence avoidance, exact Gauss support, absorption, and sufficient degree threshold are coherently tracked. The supplied exact replay matched its committed JSON byte-for-byte. I found no unresolved objection capable of invalidating a main theorem, but the contribution depends on several external antecedent theorems and its novelty is a combination claim rather than the classical local identities.
strengths: The paper explicitly prevents the common conflation of reduced fibre cardinality, scheme-theoretic fibre length, and multiplicity of the dual, with exact formulas for each.

The absorption proof uses annihilators in the correct reversed direction and obtains both the binomial local length and the Hessian ramification order d(s-1).

The prescribed-jet construction controls two analytic contact types simultaneously, avoids additional singularities and Gauss-fibre points, and explains why the stated degree threshold is sufficient rather than minimal.
The replay uses exact rational/integer arithmetic, regenerates its result in a temporary directory, and requires byte-for-byte equality with the committed results.

The novelty claim is necessarily modest because the fibre/Tjurina identity, multiplicity-Milnor formula, Hessian ramification description, and mu=tau criterion are all acknowledged as classical.
The recommendation for minor revision concerns clearer dependency and priority positioning, not a detected failure of the stated formulas.

assessments.summary: This exact 10-page PDF contains coherent, substantive specialized geometry. strengths: Lemma 2.1: equality of the value and first-jet annihilators is exactly absorption, because evaluation lines already lie in their tangent blocks. This avoids confusing ordinary Terracini defect with the much stronger value-span condition.

Lemmas 3.1-3.2: squared separators kill unwanted first jets while a local unit times a very ample section spans the retained jet. The degrees 2r-1 and 2r for double and mixed blocks are correct and work in characteristic 2 as well.

Lemmas 4.1-4.2: lambda*mu^(m-1) has a nonzero escaping tangent derivative without an m factor. Repeated escape produces d+1 independent supports, and either a further support or a common (d+1)-dimensional affine tangent space.

Lemma 5.1: multiplying a minimal-degree F by a nonvanishing complementary-degree form yields vanishing first jets. A nonzero partial contradicts minimality; if all partials vanish, perfectness gives F=G^p and radicality forces G into I. This closes the positive-characteristic loophole.

Theorems 1.2-1.3: the escape branch gives (d+1)(d+2) independent tangent directions; the Gauss branch gives binomial unisolvence. Odd m supplies q+1 double blocks and even m supplies q double blocks plus one value. The m>=2d+4 comparison holds.

Proposition 7.1 / Corollary 1.4: a product vanishing twice at p and not at q separates their tangent spaces in the complete H-embedding. Remark 1.5 correctly demonstrates why an incomplete subsystem cannot use that product section.

Lemmas 8.1-8.2 / Proposition 8.3 / Theorem 1.6: simplex interpolation, prescribed quadratic jets and Bertini produce the complex hypersurface. Degree e>m and intermediate cohomology vanishing identify the complete section space; v^(m-1) Lambda lies in the N-dimensional evaluation span.

Actual exact replays gave value/first-jet ranks 10/10 and 20/20, triple-jet rank 18, pairwise quadratic-Veronese tangent distinction and common endpoint tangents in the O(5) example. The fresh JSON agrees semantically with the supplied stored fixture record.
weaknesses: Theorem 1.6 proves existence of globally smooth hypersurfaces, not an explicit equation. The rank fixtures never construct the hypersurface or test its global singular locus; the paper states this limit correctly.

Theorems 1.2-1.3 do not classify equality cases, and the exceptional binomial examples need not minimize the global bound when the strong branch is smaller. The paper appropriately restricts its sharpness claim.

The arbitrary-characteristic novelty is localized to the reduced-set argument; jet separation and prescribed-node/Bertini methods are standard. I checked the cited Ballico-Chiantini product criterion, but did not establish exhaustive priority.

The Frobenius fixture only checks derivative coefficients of x^p+y^p. It does not computationally verify radical descent or the universal positive-characteristic statement. Confidence in that part comes from the proof, not the PASS label.

Fresh q=1,c=1 simulation at n=9421: in 20,000 Wishart draws from the strict alternative, the full band test rejected every draw and the old test rejected none. Two null cases, including a singular covariance, each had zero rejections. These are diagnostics with binomial uncertainty, not a proof of uniform level.
weaknesses: Theorem 8.1/Corollary 8.2 describe a likelihood test different from Algorithm 10. The Fisher whitening, active kernel and critical law depend on the fixed boundary K0. A practical plug-in rule and its validity across changing faces are not supplied; the demonstrated guarantee is pointwise local theory.

Section 10 provides algebraic fixture code, not a general SDP solver, dual recovery/rationalization pipeline, or constrained likelihood optimizer. The regular tangent replay checks one scalar halfspace, not noncommuting active-kernel cone projections or singular-face numerical certification.

Section 11 does not define a common sampling budget or ordering of independent-moment experiments. Its broad phrase strictly less informative should be confined to discarding the particular half-time cross block in Theorem 5.1.

The sharp normal envelope in Eq.8.10 applies to a smooth halfspace and alpha<1/2. A general spectrahedral cone projection is a likelihood-limit law, not a demonstrated uniformly most powerful test; the text mostly respects that distinction.

The Gaussian joint sketch, known zero mean, fixed finite dimension and covariance compatibility null are substantive restrictions. Alternatives with a null-representable exposed moment sequence remain undetectable by this method. The paper states these limits clearly.

Primary-source checks confirmed the matricial parity criterion and Gaussian singular-value inequality. The Geyer publisher page did not expose usable full text, and the literature search was not exhaustive; general novelty or all citation dependencies were not independently authenticated.

This is a presentational mismatch at the stated atom case, not an error in the alpha<1/2 smooth-halfspace formula.

Section 11: independent moment estimates are not intrinsically less informative without fixing acquisition and precision. The proven strict comparison is to the explicitly relaxed integer-time test on the same S; it should not be extrapolated to arbitrary independent-oracle designs.

The integrated parity-complete joint-Gram feasibility problem, active-kernel tangent description and ordinary bounded-band Farkas certificate provide an auditable workflow. The component theories themselves are established.

assessments.summary: This exact 14-page PDF contains a sound support-based Bayes ceiling under the stated physical tester normalization. I worked through the compression, Rado rank formula, prefix equality audit, positive-core correction and exact phase/Bell/trine examples; the supplied exact arithmetic suite passes after installing SymPy. I found no unresolved objection invalidating the main mathematical claims. Minor revision is warranted for the arithmetic-cost assumptions, the distinction between a bound and attainability, and repair of the incomplete release replay paths. Canonical compression and classical matroid theory are credited correctly; the useful increment is their labeled support-bound integration. The 3.8 score is a specialized contribution assessment, not an editorial decision.
strengths: Theorem 2.1, p.3: positivity of T_i<=W confines effects to supp W, so the Moore–Penrose maps are inverse and preserve all conditional probabilities. Trace(WJ_i)=1 makes the compressed operators states; arbitrary normalized positive W is not substituted for a physical deterministic tester.

Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 4.1, pp.4–5: the tagged-basis matroid-intersection argument gives min_B(|A\B|+dim sum_B S_i). The inequalities s(B)<=dim sum_B S_i^W and s_i<=1 give every rank constraint, and the common W^(1/2) map can only lower ranks.

Corollary 4.2, p.5: Abel summation with p_{M+1}=0 makes equality equivalent to simultaneous saturation only at positive prior drops, including the terminal one. Ties are handled without incorrectly forcing individual high-prior effects to be deterministic.

Theorem 4.3, p.6: each effective positive core is bounded by its support projector; residual correct mass is bounded by Tr(WR_i). Prefix summation charges at most sum_i p_i epsilon_i, preserving a valid ceiling even when exact supports jump under noise.

Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 6.1, pp.7–8: equality in the dimension bound forces each relevant positive effect onto its pure-state line, with the tie weights forming a Parseval resolution. Perfect identification additionally requires a physical W with V*WV=I, not just enough vector rank.

Theorem 8.1 and Corollary 8.2, pp.9–10: distinct phases span U_{2,L}; X/Y supply orthogonal coloops. The Bell tester attains .80 for (.30,.25,.20,.15,.10), and the completed trine POVM attains .70 for (.30,.30,.30,.10), with every trine decision nonzero.

Example 9.1, p.11: identical full-rank qubit states have true optimum .50 although the Rado bound is .80. This correctly demonstrates that support inequalities are an upper relaxation rather than a universal exact discrimination formula. The fresh exact suite checks this and the main fixtures.
weaknesses: Section 10 gives O(MR^2) for rank-one row reduction/QR without accounting for ambient input dimension m=dim H. For arbitrary m-coordinate vectors, ordinary incremental QR costs O(MmR), or requires an explicitly charged prior compression to R coordinates. The analogous mixed-support preprocessing should be stated.

Corollary 4.4 is valid but loose: convexity directly gives the stronger (1-eta)*beta+eta for common valid admixture weight eta. General positive-core selection and the supremum over deterministic W can themselves require significant optimization.

The architecture-independent upper bound is conditional on a genuinely physical normalization set D. One-slot Bell attainments neither characterize arbitrary prior chambers nor settle sequential or indefinite-order advantages with multiple slots.

The checked canonical-POVM and top-prior references substantiate those classical ingredients. The Cunningham publisher lookup failed, and the Rado-priority search was limited; this review does not certify absolute novelty or the exact cited arithmetic bound.

assessments.summary: For the exact eight-page PDF, I find a coherent and apparently correct sharp conditional theorem. The proof correctly converts point-span s-osculating absorption into order-(s+1) tangency at every point of the complete reduced Gauss fibre, applies the local Jacobian-colength bound mu >= s^d, and uses the classical dual multiplicity/tangent-cone formulas. The equality construction is carefully engineered through unisolvent points, prescribed ordinary jets, Bertini-type incidence avoidance, and a smooth extension f+yG. I found no counterexample to the stated quantifiers. Confidence is limited by the central imported tangent-floor theorem and classical dual formulas, whose full proofs were not contained in the batch, and by the deliberately nonexhaustive novelty review. These limits do not presently amount to a material objection.
strengths: Theorem 1.2 separates its four load-bearing steps: normalization gives exactly |Z| branches, Lemma 3.1 forces high contact, Lemma 4.1 supplies mu_p >= s^d, and the cited dual formulas sum the local contributions.
Lemma 4.1 uses the correct ideal inclusion J subset m^s and Hilbert-Samuel monotonicity e(J) >= e(m^s)=s^d; the ordinary initial-form case gives equality by a homogeneous regular sequence.
Theorem 1.3's construction respects every quantified d,m,s and gives an explicit sufficient degree D >= (s+2)N_{d,m}+1 while expressly avoiding a minimal-degree claim.
Proposition 6.1 checks smoothness separately off W, on W minus Z, and at Z, and its exact Gauss-fibre conclusion follows from the singular locus of the hyperplane section.
The manuscript distinguishes reduced support from the potentially nonreduced scheme fibre and avoids overstating the s=1 tangent arrangement as simple normal crossing.
weaknesses: The binomial branch floor is not proved in this PDF: Theorem 1.2 invokes the author's earlier exact tangent-absorption theorem, so correctness of the headline numerical floor is conditional on that external result.

The multiplicity identity and tangent-cone cycle formula are cited to classical sources but not independently reconstructed in full generality; the local Gauss-map calculation only recovers the ordinary equality case.
Novelty is necessarily provisional because the comparison is selective and several closest antecedents are recent papers or proof notes by the same author rather than independent literature.
The replay validates finite unisolvence, Fermat Jacobian quotients, floor arithmetic, and rank collapse, but does not test the global incidence, normalization, or duality arguments.
potential_errors: A convention mismatch in the cited tangent-cone cycle formula could change item 4 of Theorem 1.2; I found no internal sign or coefficient inconsistency, but the cited book proposition was not available in the supplied artifacts.

The normalization-to-analytic-branch step relies on completion and excellence facts that are stated tersely. For this finite birational normalization of a complex hypersurface the conclusion appears standard, but it is not expanded into a standalone lemma on completed local factors.

The incidence arguments establish nonempty open choices rather than an explicit polynomial example, so the word 'construct' should be understood existentially, consistently with the abstract's limitation.
strong_novelty_candidates: The sharp inequality mult_W(X^vee) >= s^d binom(d+m,d) obtained by coupling exact point-span absorption with the local Milnor floor.

Simultaneous equality examples with proper point span, exact reduced Gauss fibre, ordinary multiplicity-(s+1) section singularities, exact analytic-branch count, and the stated weighted tangent-cone cycle.
The observation that the earlier rank-sensitive osculating term gives no improvement for a Gauss fibre once m >= 2s+1 because the common hyperplane forces r_1(Z) <= d+1.

assessments.summary: For the exact nine-page PDF, the direct-sum occupancy law appears mathematically sound: block-dual detectors force k zeros at every wrong node, while the polynomial column F0 and matrix Fejer-Riesz normalization produce a rational-inner column with degree at most k(L-n*), and a cited state-space completion preserves that bound. The detector-rank hierarchy and three-line phase diagram also survive targeted counterexample checks. The main weakness is reproducibility packaging, not a detected theorem failure: both supplied independent verifiers terminate at missing nested certificate paths, although the two producers run, the exact detector output matches, and the numerical campaign remains within tolerance. A minor revision should repair the immutable path map and define whether floating-point reproducibility is tolerance- or byte-based.
strengths: Equations (4)-(8) give a clean gauge-invariant lower bound: each dual block detector is invertible on one target, zero on the others, and its determinant spends k boundary zeros per wrong occurrence.

Equations (9)-(13) share one degree budget across all targets: at each node only the requested polynomial block survives, direct-sum injectivity makes F0 full rank on the circle, and Fejer-Riesz normalization yields an inner column.
The cited rectangular paraunitary realization theorem supports adding channels without enlarging the state matrix, which is the exact degree-preservation needed by Lemma 3.1.
The detector-rank bound records occupancy-weighted rank deficiency for arbitrary target arrangements and reduces correctly to weighted hyperplane occupancy for lines.
Lemma 5.4 uses the Bloch-sphere circle and triple transitivity of disk automorphisms to give a credible explicit one-state construction for three distinct coplanar lines.
The collision example honestly distinguishes discontinuity of exact McMillan degree from numerical conditioning, and Theorem 6.2's Weyl-eigenvalue test fails closed.
weaknesses: Theorem 5.1's universal upper bound compresses a boundary matrix Nevanlinna-Pick construction into one paragraph without writing the Pick matrix or citing a precise theorem that guarantees regular square inner interpolation of rank k(L-1).

The reproducibility table names results/unified_routing_table_memory/certificate.json and detector_rank_certificate.json, but the exact ZIP contains only flat results/certificate.json and results/detector_rank_certificate.json.

The literature-positioning search is described as targeted and cannot support an exhaustive priority claim; the paper appropriately narrows its wording, but novelty confidence remains below theorem confidence.

Theorem 5.1's span lower bound is straightforward, but the upper bound's claimed Pick-matrix rank and regular boundary interpolation are not independently executable and are the least fully documented proof step.

Theorem 4.1 does more than state a converse: Haar mixing of the reverse exponential channel restores the exact source marginal, the stationarity equation makes the report its posterior mean, and a revealed flag attains linear faces.
Corollary 4.2 correctly expresses unrestricted squared-error RDF as the lower convex envelope of the fixed-radius Cramer cost in squared radius, making radial coexistence operationally transparent.
Proposition 5.1 derives the stability field s0=N and uses positive fourth cumulant to force a positive-radius first contact strictly before N, without claiming uniqueness or no reentrance.
Lemma 6.1 controls the drifting Bessel-weighted index with a conditioned-Poisson representation instead of interchanging a merely pointwise Weyl asymptotic with an unbounded sum.
Propositions 7.1-7.2 give mutually consistent Weyl, hypergeometric, and beta-product descriptions; the exact replay confirmed 728 dimension and complement checks and all tested cumulants.
weaknesses: The high-fidelity proof is compact enough that the uniformity used to preserve the additive constant under lower convexification deserves a separate stated lemma, even though the event split and Jensen argument point to the correct conclusion.
The equality classification in Theorem 3.2 depends on the cited Kostant-Lichtenstein quadratic criterion; the supplied batch does not contain that primary paper or a self-contained proof.
The strongest novelty claims combine several classical ingredients, and the targeted source lookup verified antecedents but was not an exhaustive field-wide search.
The figure-generation script computes the curves but then raises FileNotFoundError because src/manuscript/paper/ is absent and the script does not create it.

Theorem 4.1's endpoint completion invokes convex closure after constructing all finite-field exposed/subgradient distortions. This is standard for RDFs, but the lower-semicontinuity and zero-distortion limiting passage are not separately cited.
The figure script's output-path failure is not evidence against any theorem because the figure is expressly diagnostic, but it prevents a clean one-command reproduction of every supplied program.

assessments.summary: The exact 13-page PDF presents a substantial asymptotic analysis of a clearly classical RDF. Individual checks support the differentiated saddle constants, global contact localization, dimension-constant cancellation, convex-envelope gluing and the selected two-branch limit. Both supplied diagnostics and a separate 55-digit implementation corroborate these claims. The proof of Theorem 6.2 incorrectly asserts its raw coherent-branch expansion for all positive x; x=4a gives a direct contrary asymptotic. This does not invalidate the stated RDF, which selects the chord there, but the proof must restrict the raw calculation to its valid region. No unresolved main-claim-invalidating objection remains after that local repair. Source coverage and incidental context exposure are documented separately.
strengths: Section 3.1, p. 3: the exact Weyl product separates its m-independent C_N correction from Q_m,N. This explains why the O(N^-1) normalization term does not persist at derivative orders one and two.

Lemma 3.1, pp. 4-5: the Bessel-law mean and variance give A_p=p(p+2)/2+1/8 and B_p=2^p/sqrt(2*pi). The contact constants agree with these coefficients; the derivative claims require weighted moment control, not differentiation of an unspecified o(1).

Theorem 4.1, pp. 5-6: fixing the activation mass removes the amplified K-prime error. The fixed-b expansion correctly cancels the apparent -ab constant, which is an easy source of a false order-one term.

Lemma 5.1, p. 7: localization treats the full t/ell->1 window, including H->infinity, using the exact h-minus-hbar identity. The constant gap a(1-log(2)) excludes transition contacts competing with c=2.
Theorem 5.2, p. 8: substituting 2K=t*K-prime yields t_c=2ell+2a*log(ell)+log(4*pi)-a+o(1); a-p=1/2 cancels the representation-specific leading constant.

Proposition 5.3, pp. 8-9: the sign of b-t*K-double-prime gives convexity after contact. Combined with the global origin slope, it rules out later chords and supports unrestricted scalar-envelope attainment.
Theorems 6.1-6.2, pp. 9-10: the selected branches match in value and derivative at x=a; the fixed-D limit follows from eventual membership in the coexistence chord. D=0 is correctly excluded.

Sections 7-8: both exact-Weyl-family diagnostics ran, the broader frontier script covered the Grassmannian sequence, and Figure 1 regenerated from newly computed data rather than a stored certificate.
weaknesses: Theorem 6.2, pp. 9-10, needs a domain correction: derive the raw saddle expansion for x<a and a neighborhood of a, then use only the chord on compact sets farther to the right. Claiming both raw and line expansions uniformly on every compact subset of (0,infinity) is incorrect.

Lemma 3.1 equation (9) states two differentiated remainder bounds after a compressed moment calculation; equation (13) similarly abbreviates the reweighted variance cancellation. Give explicit moment/remainder bounds or a proved auxiliary lemma to make the uniform t>=c*ell argument readily auditable.

The exact finite-N unrestricted RDF is imported as Theorem 2.1. The moment/entropy argument is plausible and can be reconstructed, but the full public text of reference [6] was not retrieved in this assessment. No complete audit of that external theorem is claimed.

Section 8 uses "exact" for series-based floating-point K-prime and residuals. The programs truncate positive series and use floating-point roots without rigorous interval tail enclosures; the final diagnostic-only qualification should govern this wording.

README_REPRODUCIBILITY.md calls replay_all.ps1, which is absent. The individual scripts run at their supplied paths. The advertised LaTeX manuscript and bibliography are also missing from this batch; no byte-identical PDF rebuild was attempted.

The numerical contact scan detects sign-changing crossings on a finite grid; it cannot certify every stationary root or global minimality by itself. The written localization and convexity arguments remain essential.

Primary-source comparisons to Abreu, Ammari et al. and the sphere RDF were checked at abstract/metadata level only. This does not prove absence of overlapping results in their full texts or worldwide bibliographic priority.
potential_errors: Theorem 6.2 proof, p. 9: for SU(2), a=3/2 and x=4a, the asserted raw saddle t=2a*ell/x+O(1) predicts t/ell->1/2. At that field H is exponentially small, so K-prime->0, whereas sqrt(1-x/ell)->1. The actual conjugate t/ell tends to 1 (1.03290698 at N=10^200). The RDF uses the chord, so its final profile is not refuted.

Lemma 3.1, p. 4, calls the tails outside sqrt(z)*log(z) "exponentially small". The natural moderate-deviation bound is exp(-c*log(z)^2), not exp(-c*z). Superpolynomial decay suffices for the claimed algebraic remainder, but the intended rate should be stated.
strong_novelty_candidates: The global contact expansion with universal order-one constants after normalization by log(dim V_Nlambda), Theorem 5.2.
The moving-embedding classical RDF limit and matched D*log(d_N) boundary profile, with global convex-envelope gluing.
The exact activation-normalized and fixed-radius Legendre expansions that resolve the order-one cancellation in the soft window.

correctness_confidence.basis: Theorem A's spectral-factor reduction, Theorem B's Poisson-moment rigidity, Theorem C's Fourier bound, and Proposition D's square certificate are mutually consistent. The supplied 95- and 144-check audits passed, and 700 independent feasible samples violated neither displayed lower bound.

rigor.basis: The main implications are proved with explicit formulas and correctly scoped limits. The pole-exhaustion and compactness steps rely on standard Blaschke-Potapov facts, while several continuity and uniformity details are compressed rather than fully formalized.

novelty.basis: The three-parameter exact feasibility description, sharp delay-two locus, and acute-gap certificate are plausible novelty candidates. The paper expressly offers only a bounded comparison, and the public-source checks performed here cannot establish worldwide priority.

significance.basis: A complete dimension-independent reduction and sharp rigidity theorem are substantive for this tightly defined degree-two routing problem. Significance is limited by the three-node, two-state, free-phase model and by leaving the acute global optimum open.

reproducibility.basis: The two underlying symbolic audits completed with 95 and 144 checks, and the deterministic exploration ran. The advertised wrapper nevertheless terminates after those checks because public-code/paper.pdf is absent, and the exploration dependency declarations omit SciPy.

assessments.summary: For this exact nine-page PDF, I found the central algebraic and geometric arguments coherent and did not find a counterexample to the stated complete feasibility, rigidity, quantitative gap, or certified acute construction. Exact supplied audits and an independent 700-case search support the formulas but do not constitute formal verification. The main requested revision is reproducibility repair: the top-level replay cannot finish at its canonical-PDF hash step, and the numerical exploration has incomplete dependency metadata. Novelty remains plausible but only boundedly checked.
strengths: Theorem A gives a concrete necessary-and-sufficient reduction: the routed column has q(t)=t^2-d^2, a stable quadratic h(t), a nonnegative residual quadratic, and the displayed delay formula follows from h*/h.

Theorem B's equality analysis is sharp: constant peak two forces both determinant zeros to vanish, after which the boundary polynomial's maximum yields exactly a=b at least pi/2; the converse construction verifies the full locus.

Theorem C tracks the first two Fourier moments of the two Poisson kernels into a uniform denominator perturbation and an explicit positive gap, while Proposition D supplies an exact global quartic-square certificate rather than a sampled optimum.
The manuscript carefully distinguishes complete feasibility from the unresolved unrestricted acute optimum and states physical and modeling exclusions explicitly.
weaknesses: The attainment proof compresses the topology of bounded-degree Blaschke-Potapov realizations and the persistence of exact boundary interpolation in the limit; the conclusion is credible but would benefit from a fully specified compact parameterization.
The bibliography supports the classical machinery but does not establish priority for the claimed problem-specific deductions; the manuscript acknowledges this limitation.
The public replay wrapper expects public-code/paper.pdf, which is absent from the supplied batch, so it cannot produce its final report or canonical hash despite both internal audits passing.

The exploration script requires SciPy although neither research/requirements.txt nor the top-level requirements file declares it; its tolerant real-root filter also emits harmless very-large stationary points near the asymptotic value.
potential_errors: The pole-exhaustion step assumes without a local proof that equality of column and matrix McMillan degrees forces equality of every pole multiplicity and hence fixes the determinant as h*/h; the cited para-unitary theory appears relevant, but this dependency was not re-proved here.

The compactness argument ranges rank-one Potapov directions and a constant unitary over compact sets but does not explicitly discuss degenerate factorizations; I found no counterexample, yet this is the least detailed part of the existence proof.

The numerical exploration's root-imaginary tolerance can classify nearly real remote derivative roots as finite stationary points. The maximum values remained correct in the executed fixtures, so this affects diagnostics rather than the analytic propositions.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact three-real-parameter classification of all degree-two determinant-delay functions for the phase-free three-node routing table, independent of port count.
The iff characterization of delay-two attainment together with the explicit geometry-dependent positive gap outside the symmetric right-angle locus.
The cubic-root acute construction with an exact quartic-square global peak certificate and a strict improvement over the double-pole design.

correctness_confidence.basis: The common-trace orbit calculation, nine-dimensional support bound, and exact q=1/2 scalable-frame certificate are internally consistent. All three supplied scientific programs passed; a separate implementation recovered rank nine and the strict 0.005292360574691 parallel-to-causal gap.

rigor.basis: The causal upper bound and its exact attaining comb are unusually explicit. The all-pulse Bell-square and global-parallel optima rely on a terse isotypic primal-dual reduction, and collision completeness is described more exactly in prose than in the floating-point public replay.

novelty.basis: An exact analytic adaptive advantage for this non-group 24-channel family, with a rational comb saturating a family-specific rank defect, is a strong novelty candidate. Prior work already establishes sequential advantages in non-group discrimination, so the novelty is the closed family and certificate, not the general phenomenon.

significance.basis: The paper gives a transparent mechanism by which two-query chirality and coherent memory beat every parallel strategy, plus a certified open interval. Its scope is deliberately narrow: noiseless, known finite channels, two uses, and no indefinite causal order.

reproducibility.basis: The word/collision, representation, and exact quotient-field causal checks all ran successfully with pinned SymPy and NumPy. However, the supplied README names a nonexistent verification subdirectory, and package_release.py fails immediately because its compiled-PDF and other release inputs are absent.

assessments.summary: For this exact twelve-page PDF, the core result survives adversarial checking: fixed trace removes one quadratic direction, giving a nine-dimensional cap, and the explicit positive comb plus KCK=K identity attains 3/8 at q=1/2, strictly above the independently recovered global-parallel value. The principal limitations are expository and reproducibility-related rather than a found counterexample: the all-pulse primal attainment reduction is compressed, collision completeness is not machine-exact in the supplied replay, and the release helper cannot run from the provided file layout.
strengths: Theorem 6.1 uses only purification and bilinearity in two uses of the unknown qubit unitary to place every causal output in a fixed linear image of a 1+3+5 dimensional feature space, yielding the clean 9/24 cap.

Equations (12)-(16) provide a constructive deterministic comb, exact spectrum and partial trace, positive orbit weights, and an exact scalable-frame identity; the quotient-field program rechecked all 24 states and the full KCK=K relation.

Theorem 5.1 optimizes arbitrary parallel inputs including retained references by a symmetry-complete singlet/triplet marginal, and the q=1/2 solution shows explicitly why two Bell pairs are suboptimal.
Corollary 7.3 turns the point separation into an open pulse interval using a uniform derivative bound, and the manuscript clearly distinguishes ordinary causal memory from indefinite causal order.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.2 says the covariant seed operators satisfy primal completeness, but the appendix supplies only the block table and scalar reduction rather than explicit seed matrices for general pulse z; a reader must reconstruct the representation-theoretic SDP details.

The collision-completeness appendix invokes Sturm isolation and exact filtering, whereas the supplied word audit uses nroots and numerical tolerance for the final physical roots and class grouping. This leaves the exact table less reproducible than the central causal certificate.

The public layout does not match README_SUPPLIED.md: the scripts are in src/replay rather than verification, and the claimed manuscript source, bibliography, claim ledger, submission sheet, and compiled source PDF are not included at the paths required by package_release.py.

The literature check confirms that sequential advantage outside group ensembles was already known; the paper's priority claim therefore depends on its architecture-specific exact synthesis, for which no exhaustive search was performed.
potential_errors: The all-pulse Bell-square optimum depends on reducing the compound geometrically uniform discrimination SDP to one orbit weight and blockwise scalar domination. The displayed argument is plausible, but I did not independently reconstruct every attaining primal operator beyond the q=1/2 numerical fixture.

The collision table's exact completeness cannot be inferred from the executed tolerance-based classifier alone. A missed near-multiple eliminant root would affect the generic-distinctness claim, although the adaptive optimum at the isolated q=1/2 point is separately certified.
The README's replay commands and package helper cannot be followed literally on the supplied tree. This is a release-integrity error, not a mathematical counterexample to Theorem 7.2.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact global parallel formula for all pulses after optimization over arbitrary ancillary inputs, including the non-Bell optimum at q=1/2.
The fixed-trace nine-dimensional causal query defect and its exact saturation by a rational deterministic comb with positive chiral orbit weights.
The closed-form strict adaptive-versus-parallel separation for a concrete non-group unitary ensemble, extended to an explicit open pulse interval.

correctness_confidence.basis: The Weyl-Bessel constants, contact equation, dimension normalization, and matched profile are algebraically consistent and pass the supplied diagnostics plus an added SU(4) sequence. Confidence is reduced by a nontrivial unproved global-scale exclusion in Lemma 5.1 on which the later exact convex-envelope claims depend.

rigor.basis: The differentiated saddle is carefully organized, but key uniform perturbation estimates in (13) and the exclusion of radii tending to zero in Lemma 5.1 are asserted rather than bounded. The latter is material because it is used to identify and uniquely select the global contact.

novelty.basis: The dimension-normalized cancellation through order one, separated soft-activation and contact scales, and matched D log d_N boundary profile are strong novelty candidates. The search was limited to cited public primary works and cannot establish worldwide priority.

significance.basis: If the global localization is completed, the paper gives a useful universal semiclassical phase diagram for a broad highest-weight family and separates it cleanly from fixed-source high-resolution theory. The result remains conditional on the imported finite-N exact RDF theorem.

reproducibility.basis: Both deterministic diagnostics and the figure generator ran with the pinned NumPy, SciPy, and Matplotlib versions. Regenerated coherent JSON was byte-identical; frontier JSON differed only in last floating-point digits. The programs are bounded diagnostics and do not test the universal proof steps.

assessments.summary: For this exact thirteen-page PDF, the local asymptotic calculations are convincing: the Weyl factorization, Bessel saddle, contact constants, and two matched boundary branches check algebraically and numerically, including on an added SU(4) family. I cannot recommend acceptance because Lemma 5.1 does not actually supply the promised uniform exclusion of the b_N-to-zero regimes between the quadratic origin and activation window. That gap can admit an unruled-out competing slope and therefore propagates to eventual global uniqueness, exact gluing, and both main RDF limits. The cited finite-N envelope theorem was not included in the batch and was only abstract-level checked.
strengths: The exact Weyl ratio isolates an m-independent dimension factor and a uniformly small m-dependent correction, allowing the Bessel saddle to be differentiated rather than differentiating an unspecified remainder.
The contact equation 2K_N=tK_N' produces the stated log(4 pi)-a constant, and the conversion D_c=1-b_c^2 correctly turns b_c=1-a/t_c into D_c asymptotic to a/log d_N.

Theorem 6.2 matches the curved high-fidelity branch and the coexistence line in both value and derivative at x=a, with representation-specific leading constants canceling in Hilbert-dimension coordinates.

The code is explicit about being diagnostic; both supplied check programs passed, the figure regenerated, and an independent high-precision SU(4) sequence approached the displayed contact and slope constants.
weaknesses: Lemma 3.1 compresses the tilted-Weyl expectation and variance differences in equation (13) into order statements without giving the summation-by-parts or tail bounds needed for uniform first and second derivatives.

The global-localization proof treats bounded-away-from-zero radii with the fixed-b expansion, then says radii tending to zero are excluded by combining origin and subactivation estimates, without stating a uniform inequality covering that moving regime.

Theorem 2.1 is imported from another paper and only sketched. The batch contains neither that source nor a machine-verifiable substitute; public lookup confirmed only its title and abstract-level claim, not the full proof.
The diagnostics cover selected Weyl polynomials and finite grids. They cannot validate eventual uniqueness for every root system or the exact lower-convex-envelope topology.
potential_errors: A sequence with b_N tending to zero but outside the strictly quadratic and exponentially subactivated bounds is not quantitatively ruled out in Lemma 5.1. If its slope h_N were below the c=2 candidate, the claimed global contact and all downstream asymptotics would fail.

Equation (13)'s variance perturbation O((Nt)^-1) is plausible from the smooth tilt Q_m,N, but the manuscript does not show that the discrete-difference and conditioned-Poisson tail estimates remain uniform over all t at least c log d_N.

The regenerated frontier JSON is not byte-identical to the supplied frozen file, though the diff consists of approximately 1e-14 floating-point changes and every implemented tolerance passed; this is not evidence against the analytic theorem.
strong_novelty_candidates: The order-one universal contact formula in log dim V_Nlambda, with cancellation of Weyl leading constants across root systems.
The three-scale separation between soft activation, global origin-tangent contact, and the D log d_N boundary layer.
The explicit locally uniform two-branch boundary profile for the exact unrestricted classical RDF of a changing coherent-state embedding.
unresolved_material_objections: Lemma 5.1 does not provide a uniform proof excluding all b_N tending to zero between the quadratic-origin and fixed-radius regimes; it merely says the origin expansion and subactivation estimate can be combined. Because this lemma supplies global contact localization and eventual uniqueness, the omission leaves open a competing lower-slope branch and therefore blocks Theorems 5.2, 5.3, 6.1, and 6.2 as stated. A quantified interval decomposition or uniform lower bound for h_N is required.

correctness_confidence.basis: The main chain—adapted finite projection, transfer of double vanishing, the perfect-field initial-degree gap, and injective degree-m evaluation—was checked step by step without finding a counterexample or missing hypothesis under the stated algebraically closed, smooth, reduced assumptions.

rigor.basis: The kernel criterion, projection lemma, Frobenius-radical alternative, cohomology restriction, and local common-tangent calculation are explicit and mutually consistent. The Bertini and literature-priority components remain conventionally sourced rather than independently re-proved.

novelty.basis: The manuscript responsibly limits novelty to combining classical projection and fattening tools into an exact universal floor plus proper-span extremizers. Targeted source checks support the classical boundaries, but no exhaustive priority search was performed.

significance.basis: An exact codimension-free lower bound valid in every characteristic, with sharp proper-span examples for every dimension and degree, is a clean and potentially reusable structural result, though it is not a broad classification theorem.

reproducibility.basis: All three standard-library replay programs were executed. Fresh outputs matched the three committed JSON witnesses byte-for-byte and covered exact interpolation ranks, common-tangent fixtures, and exhaustive stated finite-field support grids; they do not certify Bertini or the universal proof.

assessments.summary: This exact v3 PDF gives a convincing proof that point-span tangent absorption in a complete tensor-power embedding forces rank and cardinality at least binom(d+m,d) over any algebraically closed field. The adapted projection is finite and first-order étale at the selected points; absorption transfers equality of value and double-point kernels to their images in projective d-space, where the minimal-degree derivative/Frobenius argument rules out a nonzero degree-m vanishing form. The complex common-tangent construction genuinely realizes equality with proper point span. Secondary rank and Gauss-fibre refinements also check out. Novelty is plausible but deliberately narrow and not exhaustively certified.
strengths: Theorem 1.1 isolates the exact logical chain: a center avoiding X, the selected tangent spaces, and selected secants yields a finite projection that is injective on Z with cotangent isomorphisms at every support.

Lemma 3.1 handles characteristic p correctly: if every first partial of a minimal-degree homogeneous form vanishes, perfection gives a pth root and radicality lowers the degree, contradicting minimality.
The consequence from equality in degree m to a zero value kernel is valid even when the minimal generator has lower degree, because a separate local-unit multiplier can be chosen at each support.
Theorem 1.2 is not merely ambient saturation: simplex-lattice unisolvence and a smooth hypersurface with one prescribed common tangent hyperplane give equality while h0(X,L^m) is strictly larger.
The replay suite states its finite scope accurately and reproduced all committed witnesses byte-for-byte in this execution.
weaknesses: The priority discussion is a selective bibliography rather than an exhaustive search for earlier formulations of the exact projection-plus-fattening synthesis.
Proper-span sharpness is established over C at a deliberately large sufficient hypersurface degree; positive-characteristic sharpness, minimal degree, and equality classification are not supplied.
The computational fixtures test finite ranks and local identities only; they provide no machine-checked verification of the projection, Bertini, or universal quantifiers.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact universal binomial rank floor for point-span tangent absorption over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic appears to be a strong novelty candidate as the stated synthesis of adapted projection and the symbolic-square initial-degree gap.
The proper-span equality construction for every pair (d,m), with all selected tangent hyperplanes equal, is a concrete sharpness result not located in the targeted adjacent literature checks.
The rank-sensitive first-jet and Gauss-fibre refinements are useful secondary consequences, although their ingredients are standard and their novelty was not independently certified.

correctness_confidence.basis: Euler cancellation preserves the Tjurina ideal, the truncated image-dimension estimate is valid, the plane maximization and exact families check, and the prescribed-jet surface construction is coherent. No counterexample to a main theorem was found.

rigor.basis: The local bound is self-contained and the global proof explicitly controls interpolation, off-support smoothness, the Gauss fibre, absorption, and length. The finiteness of the Gauss fibre for a smooth non-linear hypersurface is used implicitly rather than stated or justified.

novelty.basis: The sharp plane Tjurina minimum and attaining families are classical; the plausible novelty is the elementary all-germ lower count and its absorbed Gauss-fibre synthesis. Targeted primary-source checks confirm the classical boundary but do not establish exhaustive priority.

significance.basis: The work converts one Euler-forced order gain into an exact per-support plane bound and a simultaneous sharp global surface realization, a meaningful bridge between local singularity invariants and Gauss-fibre geometry.

reproducibility.basis: After installing the undeclared SymPy dependency, all finite exact checks passed. Fresh combined JSON did not match committed bytes because runtime platform and Python version are embedded; deleting only the runtime object produced exact agreement, so the mathematics reproduced but the advertised byte stability did not.

assessments.summary: This exact v2 PDF presents a sound Euler-reduced generator count for Tjurina algebras and correctly optimizes it; in dimension two it recovers the classical sharp minimum floor((3s^2+4s-3)/4) for every isolated germ of order at least s+1. The surface construction plausibly and coherently realizes the product floor on a finite Gauss fibre using prescribed contact-determined jets, incidence smoothness, and an unisolvent support. The main mathematical claims survived direct checks. Minor revision is warranted because Gauss-fibre finiteness is implicit and the replay is neither dependency-complete nor literally byte-reproducible across platforms, despite the manuscript's byte-comparison language.
strengths: Lemma 2.1 uses Euler's identity exactly where characteristic zero is needed, raises the residual generator from order s+1 to s+2, and proves equality of the original and reduced Tjurina ideals.
Theorem 2.2 bounds the image of each truncated generator separately; possible syzygies only strengthen the quotient lower bound, so no genericity or tangent-cone hypothesis is hidden in the count.
The plane quadratic optimization was checked algebraically, and the cited primary source explicitly gives the same classical minimum and the same even/odd attaining families.

Theorem 5.1 tracks enough jets for contact determinacy, uses separator products to prescribe them simultaneously, and identifies the reduced Gauss fibre with the singular locus of the tangent section.
The final equality combines exact local Tjurina lengths with the separately verified support floor rather than treating finite computations as a universal proof.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.2 does not explicitly explain why the Gauss fibre is finite; for a smooth non-linear hypersurface this follows because the Gauss pullback of O(1) is the ample O_X(deg X-1), but the length decomposition relies on that fact.
The higher-dimensional optimized number E_d,s is only a generator-count lower bound; sharpness and geometric realization are established only for d=2.
The novelty claim is necessarily narrow because the plane minimum and families are classical and the elementary local estimate may have prior commutative-algebra formulations.
The replay package omits a dependency specification for SymPy and embeds runtime metadata in the combined JSON, defeating literal cross-platform byte identity.
potential_errors: The manuscript says fresh replay JSON is compared byte-for-byte with the committed result. In this execution the mathematical payload matched exactly after deleting the runtime object, but the full bytes differed because the stored file records Windows/Python 3.12.6 and the fresh file Linux/Python 3.12.14.
strong_novelty_candidates: The Euler-reduced truncated-generator lower bound for arbitrary isolated hypersurface germs, especially its optimized higher-dimensional asymptotic, is a plausible novelty candidate subject to a fuller commutative-algebra search.
The synthesis turning osculating absorption into an exact sharp plane Gauss-fibre length floor with simultaneous proper-span surface extremizers is the strongest candidate for a new contribution.
The explicit prescribed-jet global realization at the smallest support permitted by absorption appears distinct from the classical local computation, though priority was not exhaustively established.

correctness_confidence.basis: Higher-order absorption correctly contains tangent absorption, and the block-extension, mixed-jet interpolation, incidence, connectedness, and local y-in-m^(s+1) arguments survived direct checking. The exact floor depends on the separately assessed tangent theorem, whose proof was also checked.

rigor.basis: Principal-parts definitions avoid characteristic-dependent derivative conventions, and the arbitrary-characteristic extremizer uses explicit jet-surjective incidence counts. A minor d=1 strictness sentence in the convex-packing proof should be weakened, although the lemma and downstream bound remain valid.

novelty.basis: The characteristic-free proper-span extremizers and rank-sensitive higher blocks are plausible novel contributions. The universal floor itself is an immediate reduction to the separately cited tangent theorem, and the surrounding osculating literature was checked only selectively.

significance.basis: The paper shows the tangent floor remains sharp under genuinely stronger order-s absorption in all allowed characteristics and dimensions, and supplies a useful rank-sensitive term with a sharp uniform degree threshold.

reproducibility.basis: The standard-library verifier and runner were executed successfully. Fresh results matched the committed JSON byte-for-byte and covered the stated 250-case formula grids, packing checks, rational jet blocks, finite-field unisolvence, local substitutions, and curve obstruction.

assessments.summary: This v2 paper correctly reduces the universal higher-osculating floor to the exact tangent theorem and adds nonformal sharpness under the stronger order-s condition. The arbitrary-characteristic construction is the main merit: unisolvent points exist over every algebraically closed field, and two jet-surjective incidence estimates produce a smooth integral hypersurface whose normal coordinate has order s+1 at all supports. The higher-block argument and its P1 threshold obstruction are sound. One minor proof sentence asserts strict improvement during convex packing when d=1, where equality can occur; the inequality and optimizer claim are unaffected. Priority remains selectively rather than exhaustively supported.
strengths: The intrinsic principal-parts formulation makes order-s osculating absorption meaningful without factorials and makes the reduction to tangent absorption characteristic-free.
Lemma 3.2 correctly uses e^(s+1) to annihilate old fat points and H^(m-s-1) to realize arbitrary order-s data at the new point when m is at least 2s+1.
The rational-normal-curve/P1 example genuinely disproves the uniform lambda_d(s)r1 term in every degree m at most 2s.
Proposition 6.1 replaces fragile characteristic-zero Bertini reasoning with explicit first-jet incidence codimension counts and then proves integrality from smoothness plus connectedness.
The proper-span equality argument correctly uses degree-m unisolvence on W and y in m_X,p^(s+1) to identify value and order-s kernels.
weaknesses: The exact lower floor is imported from ARR-2026-2MHNZRRJP49Y9SWP rather than proved in this paper, so the headline theorem is not logically standalone.
The proper-span construction gives an intentionally coarse sufficient degree and no canonical equation, minimal-degree analysis, or classification of equality cases.
The priority comparison with higher osculating, secant, and subspace-rank literature is selective and cannot support an exhaustive novelty claim.
potential_errors: In Lemma 4.3's proof, moving weight between two nontrivial blocks is said to strictly increase the objective; for d=1 the forward differences are constant, so it may only preserve it. The stated upper bound and existence of the packed optimizer still follow from nondecrease.
strong_novelty_candidates: Characteristic-free proper-span equality examples for every (d,m,s), realized by smooth hypersurfaces with a shared hyperplane of prescribed order-s contact, are a strong novelty candidate.
The rank-sensitive higher-block estimate lambda_d(s)r1(Z) for m at least 2s+1, together with its uniform sharp-threshold obstruction on P1, is a clear candidate for a new refinement.
The corrected hierarchy separating the exact tensor-power floor from the older mixed-jet certificate is mathematically useful, though the underlying interpolation devices are classical.

correctness_confidence.basis: Theorems 2.1, 4.1, 5.1-5.3, 6.1-6.2, 7.1-7.2, and 8.1-8.11 were checked claim by claim. Their central algebra and probability arguments are coherent; independent numerical checks found no counterexample, but the longest Gaussian-process and concentration proofs remain compressed rather than independently rederived in full detail.

rigor.basis: Hypotheses and claim boundaries are unusually explicit, and most constants trace to displayed inequalities. Theorem 8.11 compresses its uniform-over-angle overlap and Gaussian-bridge transfer into standard-result invocations, while the Cramer-Rao qualification appears only later in the limitations section.

novelty.basis: The manuscript carefully disclaims the classical Schwarzian criterion, one-unit Fisher split, known logistic exponents, and scaled-SVD mechanism. Limited primary-source checks support those boundaries; the exact bridge coefficient, three-phase constants, lexicographic angle law, and angular-log obstruction remain credible novelty candidates, not established priority guarantees.

significance.basis: The paper unifies matrix-order failure, population saturation geometry, sharp fixed-teacher oracle-Gram resolution, and extreme-saturation eigenspaces in one analytically tractable neuron. Its scope is deliberately local, oracle, and mostly Gaussian or spherical, limiting immediate estimator or deep-network impact.

reproducibility.basis: All 19 public-code files match PUBLIC-CODE-MANIFEST.json, and seven of nine scripts ran successfully under available nearby package versions. Exact pinned packages were unavailable and python-flint was missing; moreover four supplied JSON certificates do not match the README's declared deterministic hashes, so exact replay is unresolved.

assessments.summary: This exact v5 artifact is a substantial, technically ambitious synthesis with several credible original refinements. I found no unresolved objection that presently invalidates a main theorem: the logistic Loewner determinant, spherical/Gaussian saturation laws, all-power moments, fixed-oracle concentration scale, and spectral hierarchy are mutually consistent, and targeted independent checks did not find counterexamples. The main required revision is reproducibility hygiene: the README's expected hashes disagree with four supplied manifest-verified certificates, the exact pinned environment could not be instantiated here, and the Arb-dependent witness was not re-executed. Novelty confidence is bounded by a limited primary-source search, especially for the newest spectral and angular-process claims. This is a referee assessment, not an editorial decision.
strengths: Theorem 2.1 gives a clean closed determinant identity and correctly separates its explicit logistic specialization from the classical order-two Schwarzian criterion and serial-composition law.
Theorems 4.1 and 5.1-5.3 expose the transition-layer mechanism with exact constants, including the inverse-radius phase boundary and a concrete covariance-isotropy counterexample.

Theorem 6.1 links the adjacent-point Loewner defect to radial-tangential anisotropy through an exact fourth-moment multiplier, and Theorem 6.2 turns the limit identity into a finite-scale error bound.

assessments.summary: This exact nine-page v3 presents a convincing exact rank theorem in arbitrary characteristic. I checked the projection avoidance conditions, finiteness argument, minimal-degree fattening gap including the all-partials-zero case, rank transfer, complex sharpness construction, and secondary block/Gauss refinements. strengths: Lemma 3.1 (p. 4): double vanishing implies every homogeneous partial vanishes on Y. A nonzero derivative contradicts least degree; if all partials vanish, perfection gives F=G^p and radicality lowers the degree. The local-unit multiplication argument correctly extends the contradiction to equality of kernels in arbitrary degree m.

Lemma 4.1 (p. 4): a general center avoids X, finitely many d-dimensional tangent spaces and finitely many secants. A positive-dimensional projective fibre would meet the center hyperplane, contradicting disjointness. Thus the projection is finite and has the required tangent isomorphisms.

Theorem 1.1 (pp. 4-5): at zeros of F, the cotangent isomorphism transfers second-order vanishing from its pullback. Injective degree-m evaluation on Y then injects a binomial-dimensional evaluation subspace on Z, with no projective-normality assumption.

Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 1.2 (pp. 5-6): the falling-factorial matrix is triangular with unit diagonal over C. With n>m, every section lifts uniquely; vanishing on Z forces divisibility by y, and y=-f/G belongs to m_p^2. This gives equality with a genuinely proper point span.

Proposition 7.1 (p. 6): the system is base-point-free off Z, characteristic-zero Bertini applies there, and nonzero G(p) gives smoothness at every base point. Reducible positive-dimensional projective hypersurfaces would have intersecting components and be singular.

Propositions 8.2-8.3 and Corollary 8.4 (p. 7): squared separators require m>=3; downward propagation forces r1>=d+1. Equality puts all supports in one Gauss fibre, yielding the stated alternative. The smooth-quadric polar-radical argument also works on geometric points in characteristic two.

Section 10: fresh replay stdout records the 20 deletion-boundary fixtures, six local common-tangent fixtures, and exhaustive 7,15,127-support checks on P^1(F2), P^1(F3), P^2(F2). All three byte comparisons succeeded; no source-hashing failure occurred.

The novelty comparison should engage explicitly with subspace rank, beyond Terracini and strong-base-locus terminology. Ballico defines rank by containment in a reduced point span and studies tangent-containing spaces: https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2013/4/4.pdf. This does not itself prove the present simultaneous theorem.

strengths: Lemma 1, p.3: the relation lattice lies in qZ^2, giving |H|=q^2h. Trace orthogonality forces equal central-sector dimensions, and unitary eigenvalue cycling supplies exactly m equivalent q-dimensional copies.

Theorem 3, pp.5-6: the noncommuting and commuting alternatives exhaust supports after right normalization. Binomials realize each p^j corank, and the odd-order quadratic realizes each additional 2p^j corank.

Proposition 4 and (6a)-(6c), pp.6-7: the d=12 nullity-three case, d=36 nullity-six sharp case and zero-constant control separately test multiplicity, two-sector sharpness and the necessary coefficient hypothesis.

assessments.summary: This exact 14-page paper derives a valid support-sensitive Bayes ceiling for general quantum testers. Moore-Penrose compression preserves the entire conditional-probability table; correct-label probabilities then satisfy every Rado independence-polytope inequality, so greedy maximum-weight transversal mass bounds success. The robust low-rank-core correction, equality audit, Gram feasibility condition, exact phase-flat chamber, trine-plus-coloop construction, and mixed full-rank counterexample are mutually consistent. I found no unresolved objection capable of invalidating the main bound. The recommended revision is driven by the incomplete release payload and environment-dependent figure hashes, plus the inherently limited evidence for first-priority claims.
strengths: Theorem 2.1 handles singular tester normalizations correctly: support inclusion makes the Moore-Penrose maps inverse on supp W, and cyclicity preserves every conditional probability rather than only Bayes success.

Theorem 4.1's key subset inequality is sound: each effective density is bounded by the projector onto the joint support, and singleton caps plus Rado's rank formula place the correct-label vector in the full independence polytope.
Corollary 4.2 uses Abel summation correctly, requiring saturation only at prefixes followed by a strict prior drop, including the terminal drop; ties do not receive spurious conditions.

Theorem 4.3 validly separates positive cores from residuals and telescopes the prior-weighted tester-mass errors, avoiding the discontinuity of exact support under arbitrarily small full-rank admixture.

The phase-flat and trine-plus-coloop examples attain the matroid ceiling by explicit normalized Choi-state POVMs, while Example 9.1 honestly demonstrates that support data do not generally determine a mixed-state optimum.
The supplied exact SymPy verifier passed its singular compression, mixed Rado, robust spectral-tail, prior-profile, Gram, and trine fixtures.
weaknesses: For mixed processes the support matroid can be very loose; useful application depends on choosing positive low-rank cores and bounding their worst-case discarded tester mass, neither of which the method optimizes.
The phase-family exactness chamber relies on Bell-resolvable anchors I and Z carrying the two largest phase priors; arbitrary top-prior phase pairs need not attain the support ceiling.
The claimed practical complexity invokes repeated linear matroid intersection and exact or certified rank decisions; no general implementation or scaling benchmark is supplied.

The novelty assessment remains bounded by targeted primary-source searches covering canonical testers, general unitary discrimination, and prior-weighted state bounds, not an exhaustive quantum-decision-theory survey.

assessments.summary: This exact 12-page manuscript gives a mathematically coherent structured-Wishart test for compatibility with a matrix-valued measure supported on [0,s]. The parity-complete Hausdorff cone, single simultaneous Loewner band, and shared moment variables deliver finite-sample level without multiplicity correction. The two-atom family genuinely separates the older integer-grid condition from the full half-time constraint on the same covariance, and the supplied exact dual independently certifies the population rejection. The tangent-cone and local likelihood conclusions are plausible applications of standard constrained-likelihood theory, though their proof is terse. No material counterexample was found; a minor revision should make the asymptotic regularity and metric identifications more explicit.
strengths: Theorem 3.1 states the correct parity-dependent matricial Hausdorff conditions, including rank-deficient sequences, and the paper uses the even criterion appropriate to the acquired H_q covariance.

Theorem 4.1 obtains level control from one Gaussian singular-value event: the true structured covariance is feasible throughout that event, so adaptive inspection of all moment witnesses adds no multiple-testing penalty.

Theorem 5.1 is a genuine same-acquisition separation. For the two-atom measure, s^2M0-M2 is positive while sM1-M2 is negative, and the nuclear-norm support calculation yields an explicit sample threshold.

Theorem 7.1 correctly treats H_q positivity as inactive at K0 positive definite and compresses the active localizer to its kernel; the positive-density direction supplies the needed linearized Slater condition.

Proposition 9.1 avoids treating floating-point infeasibility as proof. Injectivity of the Hankel map plus the bounded Loewner sandwich rules out weak infeasibility and supports an ordinary separating certificate.
The exact replay passed every advertised algebraic fixture, including noncommuting 2x2 weights, the -3/128 dual objective, strict old/full margins, and the smooth-face local-power illustration.
weaknesses: The operational model requires iid, zero-mean Gaussian joint exponent sketches. The paper does not provide a corresponding validated acquisition for sub-Gaussian, dependent, or raw Monte Carlo observations.
The finite truncation tests only the exposed covariance cone; alternatives sharing all acquired moments with a supported measure remain undetectable, as the manuscript acknowledges.

The LAN and cone-likelihood proof compresses stochastic uniformity, scaled-set convergence, and the Fisher whitening identification into a short appeal to standard theory; readers must reconstruct these conditions from Chernoff/Shapiro-style results.
The public-code replay checks algebraic fixtures but does not simulate coverage, solve a range of numerical SDPs, or validate scientific data, limiting empirical reproducibility claims.

Targeted primary-source checks confirmed classical matricial Hausdorff and inequality-constrained likelihood antecedents but were not exhaustive enough to prove first priority for the integrated test.
potential_errors: Theorem 8.1 reuses closely similar K0 notation for the base covariance and the whitened tangent cone; this is editorially hazardous in the displayed likelihood limit and should be disambiguated, although the intended geometry is recoverable.

Theorem 8.3's detection statement is stronger than the fixed-distance consistency theorem cited in its proof. It is supportable by choosing a high-probability covariance radius o(dist(K_n,C)), but that vanishing-distance argument should be written explicitly.

The local likelihood conclusion depends on positive definiteness and linearized Slater at the active face; more singular intersections are outside the theorem, so the phrase sharp tangent-cone power should not be generalized beyond those regular points.
strong_novelty_candidates: The single joint half-time Gaussian acquisition whose complete covariance enforces every anti-diagonal identity and uses cross-exponent blocks in one parity-complete support test.
The explicit two-atom family proving finite-sample power separation between the full joint test and the precisely defined predecessor integer-grid test on the same observations.
The combination of an exact active-kernel tangent preimage, Gaussian cone-projection local law, and ordinary auditable SDP rejection certificate for the structured moment cone.
